description: The is a cytogenetic case study of a 10-year-old female with pure pigmented dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans (DFSP), also called Bednar tumor, on her right shoulder. Karyotype of tumor cells was 47,XX with 2 copies of der(22)t(17;22)(q22;q13). BAC clones mapping to 22q13.1 at the PDGFB locus, and 17q21.33 at the COL1A1I locus and used as FISH probes detected COL1A1-PDGFB gene fusion on the derivative der(22) chromosomes. RT-PCR and Sanger sequencing narrowed down the fusion to exon 41 of COL1A1 and exon 2 of PDGFB. Adult Bednar and DFSP tumors typically show ring chromosomes composed of der(22) material, while pediatric DFSP tumors show a linear structural abnormality of an unbalanced translocation t(17;22)(q22;q13). This is the first reported pediatric case of a pure Bednar tumor with a linear chromosomal structural abnormality involving chromosomes 22 and 17, in addition to having a normal chromosome 22 and two normal chromosomes 17. The COL1A1 breakpoint at exon 41 in the COL1A1-PDGFB fusion gene is newly reported in this case study and reaffirms the known variability in COL1A1 breakpoints spanning exons 6-49.
name: EID12416

source.title: COL1A1-PDGFB fusion in a pediatric Bednar tumor with 2 copies of a der(22)t(17;22).

description: The authors studied 27 archival formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) samples of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans (DFSP) cases obtained from Texas Children's Hospital and University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center. The cases included 16 females and 11 males with an age range of 1-73 years and diagnosed with DFSP and diffuse expression of CD34 by immunohistochemistry. Using a highly sensitive multiplex RT-PCR-direct sequencing assay developed for FFPE tissue, the authors detected COL1A1-PDGFB fusion transcripts with 18 different COL1A1 forward primers spanning the α-helical domain (exons 5-49) and a single PDGFB reverse primer. Break-apart FISH was performed using BAC DNA clones mapping centromeric and telomeric of the PGDFB locus. Sequencing analysis confirmed in-frame fusion of exon 2 of PDGFB to different breakpoints in COL1A1 (exons 7, 10, 29, 40, 46, and 49 and introns between exons 13:14, 26:27, 30:31, 33:34, 43:44, 45:46, 46:47). Of these, COL1A1 breakpoints in exon 49 and in introns between exons 13:14 and 30:31, are novel. Using both RT-PCR and FISH techniques, the authors report a higher prevalence of COL1A1-PDGFB rearrangements (96%) in DFSP cases than reported in earlier studies, and attribute this to the high sensitivity of their multiplex RT-PCR direct sequencing assay. Testing FFPE specimen with both FISH and RT-PCR would prove helpful for the differential diagnosis of atypical, fibrosarcomatous and metastatic DFSP.
name: EID12417

source.title: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans COL1A1-PDGFB fusion is identified in virtually all dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans cases when investigated by newly developed multiplex reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction and fluorescence in situ hybridization assays.

description: In this study, paraffin-embedded tissue microarray (TMA) evaluation of translocation t(17;22)(q22;q13) was performed on 40 tissue samples from 24 female and 16 male DFSP patients (37 primary tumors, 3 local recurrences) obtained from 3 hospitals in Barcelona, Spain. The median age of these DFSP patients was 43 y and the age range was 15-87 y. A second tissue microarray included 20 samples from dermatofibroma (DF) patients. Samples from 6 postsurgical scars were used as negative controls. FISH was performed using dual-color dual-fusion BAC clones to detect the cytogenetic COL1A1-PDGFB translocation. From the evaluable 29 DFSP cases, 86% (n=25) showed the COL1A1-PDGFB FISH signal pattern, which was absent in all DF control cases and in the 6 scars. Of these 25 COL1A1-PDGFB positive DFSP cases, 19 showed multiple (more than 3) copies of the translocation. Tumor size correlated positively with a higher proportion of DFSP tumor cells showing the fusion signal, and DFSPs with fibrosarcomatous areas (DFSP-FS) also showed cells with 6 or more COL1A1-PDGFB gene fusions signals.
name: EID12418

source.title: Identification of t(17;22)(q22;q13) (COL1A1/PDGFB) in dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans by fluorescence in situ hybridization in paraffin-embedded tissue microarrays.

description: This study provided in vivo evidence showing the adipocyte-specific oncogenicity of the FUS::CHOP fusion transcript in liposarcoma, using a transgenic mouse model with ubiquitous FUS::CHOP expression driven by the elongation factor 1a (EF1a) promoter. These mice uniformly developed liposarcoma without sex bias and exhibited characteristic symptoms similar to those in human liposarcoma. No tumors were detected in other tissues. Mechanistically, FUS::CHOP expression in vivo blocked adipocyte differentiation by inducing the expression of the nuclear receptor peroxisome proliferative-activated receptor gamma (PPARg). The study provides evidence that the FUS::DDIT3 fusion acts as the primary oncogenic driver in myxoid liposarcoma (MLS) and is thus a suitable diagnostic marker for this tumor type.
name: EID12430

source.title: The chimeric FUS/TLS-CHOP fusion protein specifically induces liposarcomas in transgenic mice.

description: This preclinical study examined the effect of the FUS::DDIT3 fusion protein on the oncogenic role of IGF-1R/PI3K/Akt signaling in myxoid liposarcoma (MLS) and explored the therapeutic potential of IGF-1R inhibitors, including NVP-AEW541 in this disease. Immunohistochemistry (IHC) revealed elevated expression and activating phosphorylation of various components in the IGF-1R signaling pathway in MLS clinical specimens (n=60). Overexpression of FUS::DDIT3 in HT1080 fibrosarcoma cells induced IGF2-IGF-1R/PI3K/Akt activation. Topical administration of NVP-AEW541 onto MLS xenograft tumors on the chick chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) was found to significantly suppress tumor growth in vivo (p<0.05). The study shows that the FUS::DDIT3 fusion drives oncogenic program in MLS; it is a defining abnormality and a suitable diagnostic marker for this tumor type.
name: EID12431

source.title: FUS-DDIT3 Fusion Protein-Driven IGF-IR Signaling is a Therapeutic Target in Myxoid Liposarcoma.

description: In this retrospective multicenter study, 218 patients diagnosed with B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (B-ALL) harboring ZNF384 rearrangements were analyzed between 1992 and 2018 across 16 international consortia. ZNF384 rearrangements were found in about 5% of pediatric and 10% of adult B-ALL cases and were mutually exclusive with other well-defined genetic subtypes. FISH), RT-PCR, and NGS identified ZNF384 fusion transcripts with partners such as EP300, TCF3, TAF15, and CREBBP. Detection of ZNF384 fusions was critical for classifying B-ALL cases lacking other recurrent cytogenetic abnormalities. EP300::ZNF384 fusions showed a distinct clinical profile, including older age at diagnosis and favorable outcomes, while other ZNF384 rearrangements exhibited unique immunophenotypic features like aberrant myeloid marker expression (CD13, CD33). These findings highlight the diagnostic importance of ZNF384 rearrangements in B-ALL and support their recognition as a distinct molecular entity.

disease.name: B-lymphoblastic Leukaemia/lymphoma With Other Defined Genetic Alterations

name: EID12440

source.title: Clinical characteristics and outcomes of B-ALL with ZNF384 rearrangements: a retrospective analysis by the Ponte di Legno Childhood ALL Working Group.

description: In this study, the authors investigated a targeted diagnostic approach to identify ZNF384 rearrangements in B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (B-ALL)  based on immunophenotypic features. Since ZNF384 fusions are often cryptic and linked to dim CD10 expression and aberrant CD13/CD33 expression, 109 B-ALL patients with <80% CD10 expression and negative BCR-ABL1 status were screened. ZNF384 rearrangements were found in 14 cases, with EP300::ZNF384 as the most common fusion. Flow cytometry screening, FISH followed by RT-PCR and Sanger sequencing identified further fusion partners including EP300, TAF15, and TCF3. Recognizing ZNF384 fusions is particularly valuable for diagnosing B-ALL cases that do not harbor other defining cytogenetic or molecular alterations.

disease.name: B-lymphoblastic Leukaemia/lymphoma With Other Defined Genetic Alterations

name: EID12442

source.title: Systematic application of fluorescence in situ hybridization and immunophenotype profile for the identification of ZNF384 gene rearrangements in B cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia.

description: A cross-sectional cohort study was performed in 161 men with metastatic prostate cancer undergoing a change in treatment to determine if pre-therapy AR-V7 nuclear protein expression in circulating tumor cells (CTCs) is a treatment-specific marker for outcomes between androgen receptor signaling (ARS) inhibitors and taxanes. A multivariable model adjusting for baseline factor associated with survival showed superior overall survival with taxanes relative to ARS inhibitors when AR-V7-positive CTCs were detected pre-therapy (hazard ratio , 0.24; 95% CI 0.10-0.57; P=0.035).
name: EID12463

source.title: Association of AR-V7 on Circulating Tumor Cells as a Treatment-Specific Biomarker With Outcomes and Survival in Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer.

description: A blinded, multi-institutional cohort study was performed in 142 men with metastatic, castration-resistant prostate cancer to determine if pre-therapy nuclear-localized expression of AR-V7 protein in circulating tumor cells (CTCs) is a treatment-selective marker for outcome following treatment with either androgen receptor signaling (ARS) inhibitors or taxanes. Patients with AR-V7-positive CTCs had superior overall survival with taxanes vs ARS inhibitors (hazard ratio 0.62; 95% CI 0.28-1.39; P=.25). Patients with AR-V7-negative CTCs had superior overall survival with ARS inhibitors vs taxanes (hazard ratio 1.67; 95 CI 1.00-2.81); P=.05).
name: EID12464

source.title: Assessment of the Validity of Nuclear-Localized Androgen Receptor Splice Variant 7 in Circulating Tumor Cells as a Predictive Biomarker for Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer.

description: To compare the activity of AR-V7 with that of full-length AR (AR-FL) lentiviral stable cell lines of castrate-resistant prostate cancer were generated that expressed doxycycline-regulated AR-V7 or AR-FL using the cell line C4-2 PCa. These cells were injected into the tibias of castrated male mice. Compared to cells expressing or over-expressing AR-FL those expressing AR-V7 induced mixed osteoblastic/osteoclastic bone lesions and increased the area of bone lesions 4-6 weeks after injection. Expression of SOX9 protein, a known driver of metastasis, increased significantly in tumors expressing AR-V7 but remained low and unchanged in those expressing AR-FL.
name: EID12465

source.title: Androgen receptor splice variants drive castration-resistant prostate cancer metastasis by activating distinct transcriptional programs.

description: In this 2017 study, the authors analyzed 91 pediatric B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia (BCP-ALL) patients and an additional 122 classified as "B-others" lacking conventional genetic abnormalities. ZNF384 rearrangements were identified through whole transcriptome sequencing and PCR-based fusion detection. ZNF384-related fusions were detected in 4.1% of all BCP-ALL cases (9.2% of B-others), with TCF3::ZNF384 being most frequent (2.4% overall). The leukemic cells exhibited a characteristic immunophenotype of weak/absent CD10 and aberrant CD13/CD33 expression, distinct from ZNF384-fusion negative cases. Gene expression profiling revealed enrichment of hematopoietic stem cell features in TCF3::ZNF384 cases, differing from TCF3-PBX1-positive ALL. Clinically, TCF3-ZNF384 patients presented with higher leukocyte counts and poorer steroid response compared to EP300-ZNF384 cases, suggesting fusion partner-dependent heterogeneity. The study demonstrates that ZNF384 rearrangements define a molecularly distinct BCP-ALL subgroup with diagnostic immunophenotypic features, while clinical outcomes vary by fusion partner.

disease.name: B-lymphoblastic Leukaemia/lymphoma With Other Defined Genetic Alterations

name: EID12466

source.title: ZNF384-related fusion genes define a subgroup of childhood B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia with a characteristic immunotype.

description:
Fibroblast Growth Factor Receptor 1 (FGFR1) amplification is frequently observed in estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) breast cancer and is associated with poor prognosis and resistance to endocrine therapy. FGFR inhibitors have shown potential to overcome this resistance. 
A phase II study, the NCI-MATCH ECOG-ACRIN Trial (EAY131) Subprotocol K1 (NCT06308822), was an open-label, single-arm trial that required central confirmation of FGFR1–4 amplification in tumors. A total of 18 patients were enrolled, including 9 with breast cancer. FGFR amplifications were detected by the NCI-MATCH sequencing assay, with a minimum laboratory reported copy number of 7.0. All participants received oral erdafitinib at a starting dose of 8 mg once daily, with dose escalation to 9 mg permitted based on tolerability.
The primary endpoint was the centrally assessed objective response rate (ORR). Key secondary endpoints included 6-month progression-free survival (PFS6), overall PFS, overall survival (OS), and safety.
No confirmed responses to erdafitinib were observed. However, five patients achieved stable disease as their best response. Notably, one patient with FGFR1-amplified breast cancer experienced prolonged survival, with a PFS exceeding 168 days (5.5 months).
name: EID12469

source.title: Phase II Study of Erdafitinib in Patients With Tumors With FGFR Amplifications: Results From the NCI-MATCH ECOG-ACRIN Trial (EAY131) Subprotocol K1.

description: In this study, the authors used long-distance inverse PCR and sequencing to comprehensively analyze KMT2A (MLL) gene rearrangements in 2,345 acute leukemia patients, including those with B-lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL). The findings reinforce the diagnostic significance of KMT2A rearrangements in B-ALL, particularly in infants and young children. The study identified 135 distinct KMT2A rearrangements involving 94 translocation partner genes (TPGs); of those, only 9 fusions accounted for over 90% of the cases, including KMT2A::AFF1, KMT2A::MLLT1, and KMT2A::MLLT3. Among B-ALL patients, the KMT2A::AFF1 (AF4) fusion was the most frequent, especially in infants, followed by KMT2A::MLLT1 (ENL) and KMT2A::MLLT3 (AF9). Importantly, the study highlighted an age-dependent breakpoint shift within the KMT2A locus, with intron 11 breakpoints associated more frequently with B-ALL in younger patients, and intron 9 breakpoints found more often in AML and older patients. This study supports the classification of B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with KMT2A rearrangement as a distinct diagnostic entity independent of the fusion partner; this is recognized in the WHO 5th edition (2022) and the International Consensus Classification.
name: EID12473

source.title: The MLL recombinome of acute leukemias in 2017.

description:
In this publication, the authors conducted a comprehensive genomic analysis of 2,754 pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) cases using integrated whole genome, exome, and transcriptome sequencing. Of the 2,288 B-ALL cases analyzed, KMT2A rearrangements were identified in approximately 4.5%, confirming their role as a recurrent driver in pediatric B-ALL. These KMT2A-rearranged cases were characterized by a low somatic mutational burden, distinct gene expression profiles, and unique biological features compared to other B-ALL subtypes.
The study revealed multiple KMT2A fusion partners, with recurrent fusions involving genes such as MLLT1, MLLT3, AFF1, and others, reinforcing that the diagnostic significance lies in the presence of the KMT2A rearrangement itself, irrespective of the fusion partner. Further sub-classification based on transcriptome clustering identified two transcriptionally distinct KMT2A subgroups—one enriched for NFATC4 expression and the other for CEBPA/FLT3 expression—suggesting underlying differences in developmental origin and potential clinical implications.
These findings support the recognition of B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with KMT2A rearrangement as a distinct diagnostic entity, consistent with the updated 2022 International Consensus Classification (ICC) and the 2024 World Health Organization (WHO) classification.
name: EID12474

source.title: The genomic landscape of pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia.

description:
In this publication, the diagnostic significance of KMT2A rearrangements in B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (B-ALL) is explored. The study reveals that KMT2A fusions are not restricted to lymphoid lineages but may also involve myeloid compartments and hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells (HSPCs), supporting a multilineage origin in a substantial proportion of cases. Notably, 36% of patients with KMT2A-rearranged B-ALL exhibited evidence of multilineage involvement at diagnosis.

This finding has important diagnostic implications, as conventional MRD assessment strategies—relying on flow cytometry or immunoglobulin gene rearrangement—may fail to detect residual disease in cases where leukemic clones persist in non-lymphoid compartments. RNA sequencing data further demonstrate a gene expression profile enriched for HSPC and myeloid programs in these patients, reinforcing the hybrid lineage biology of KMT2A-rearranged B-ALL. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating molecular techniques such as fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) or RNA-based assays to detect KMT2A fusions as key diagnostic markers in this B-ALL subtype.
name: EID12475

source.title: Multilineage involvement in KMT2A-rearranged B acute lymphoblastic leukaemia: cell-of-origin, biology, and clinical implications.

description: Dovitinib, a pan-FGFR small molecular inhibitor, has shown activity in pre-clinical models against FGFR-expressing breast cancer model cell lines, as well as as in a single agent in a phase II clinical trial in HR+/HER2- FGFR1 amplified breast cancer patients. Notably, this is among patients with higher levels of FGFR amplification. A phase II, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial was designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of dovitinib in combination with fulvestrant in postmenopausal women with HR+, HER2− locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer with disease progression. FGF pathway amplification was determined using TaqMan assay as described by (André F. et al, 2013). Positive amplification for each FGF pathway marker tested (i.e., FGFR1, FGFR2, or FGF3) was defined as a copy number ≥6. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS). However, the study had to be stopped early due to slow accrual of patients with FGF pathway amplification. The overall response rate (assessed at regular radiological assessment) in the dovitinib + fulvestrant arm (n=47) was 27.7%, as compared to 10% in the placebo + fulvestrant arm (n=50), irrespective of the presence of FGF pathway amplification. The FGFR-amplified subgroup (n=31) reached a median PFS of 10.9 months vs 5.5 months in the dovitinib + fulvestrant vs placebo + fulvestrant arms respectively. The final analysis showed limited benefit, with the authors' recommendation to exercise caution when interpreting the study results (particularly the PFS results), due to a fewer than expected number of PFS events (18 vs 50 planned events), as well as the study's small sample size.
name: EID12478

source.title: Phase II, randomized, placebo-controlled study of dovitinib in combination with fulvestrant in postmenopausal patients with HR+, HER2- breast cancer that had progressed during or after prior endocrine therapy.

description: The Targeted Agent and Profiling Utilizing Registry (TAPUR) study is a prospective, phase II, basket trial that aims to evaluate the antitumor activity of commercially available targeted therapies prescribed to patients with advanced cancer with actionable targets. In this study, sunitinib is evaluated in patients with breast cancer, with FGFR alterations. Patients eligible for the study include those age 12 years or older, who have BC with an FGFR1/2 amplification or mutation. Definitions of amplification were not prespecified in the protocol because of the variety of genomic tests that could qualify a patient for participating in the study. The primary endpoint was disease control (DC) based on the investigator assessment – this was defined as objective response (OR) or stable disease (SD) of at least 16 weeks duration (SD16+), measured from the initiation of study treatment, as determined by the Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) version 1.1. Secondary endpoints were progression free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), duration of response, duration of SD, and safety. Thirty patients with BC with FGFR1 alterations (amplification = 26, mutation = 1, both amp + mut = 3) were initially enrolled. Due to patient ineligibility and drop out, 27 patients were evaluable for sunitinib efficacy (amp=26, mut=1). With regards to DC, two patients were reported with partial response and four with SD16+ were observed for DC. The DC rate was calculated to be 27% (90% CI, 13 to 100) and OR to be 7% (95% CI, 1 to 24). The median PFS was 9 weeks in the FGFR1 cohort (95% CI, 8 to 16). Given the null hypothesis of a 15% DC rate was not rejected, sunitinib did not meet the study’s thresholds for demonstrating antitumor activity in patients with BC harboring FGFR1 amplifications. The study concludes that sunitinib is not recommended for off-label use in FGFR1-altered BC.
name: EID12479

source.title: Sunitinib in Patients With Breast Cancer With FGFR1 or FGFR2 Amplifications or Mutations: Results From the Targeted Agent and Profiling Utilization Registry Study.

description: PALOMA-3, a phase III, multicenter, double-blind randomized controlled trial enrolled patients with advanced estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer receiving fulvestrant (estrogen receptor antagonist) therapy with either palbociclib (a CDK4/6 inhibitor) (N = 347) or placebo (N = 174). Of the total number of 459 patients, 401 patients had enough DNA in pretreatment plasma samples for a custom targeted sequencing panel to assess for mutations  (17 genes), copy number alterations (14 genes), and circulating tumor fraction. The prevalence of copy number alterations was assessed only in samples with more than 10% circulating tumor fraction (N=156). Gain of copy number of FGFR1 was observed in 10% (15/156) as one of the most frequent finding, together with gains of MCL1, CCND1, and MYC. In univariable analysis gains in FGFR1 were associated with poorer progression-free survival (PFS) in both treatment groups [HR=3.40, 95% CI 1.91. to 6.04, log-rank Q<0.001 for the group treated with palbociclib plus fulvestrant, and HR = 3.61, 95% CI = 1.31 to 9.97; log-rank Q=0.047 for the group treated with fulvestrant with placebo]. Since an increased circulating tumor fraction was required to detect copy number changes in plasma and higher circulating tumor fraction was also associated with worse PFS, a multivariable analysis was performed. FGFR1 gain remained statistically significant in the model [HR=2.91, 95% CI 1.61 to 5.25, p<0.001]. The median PFS of patients on palbociclib and fulvestrant with detected FGFR1 gain was 3.9 months vs 12.0 months for those without it. In addition, PFS of patients with FGFR1 gain together with TP53 mutations was at 3.7 months. There was no statistically significant interaction for FGFR1 gain with treatment randomization.
name: EID12486

source.title: Circulating Tumor DNA Markers for Early Progression on Fulvestrant With or Without Palbociclib in ER+ Advanced Breast Cancer.

description:
This study aimed to determine the amplification rates of FGFR1, FGFR2, and FGFR3 in breast cancer and evaluate their impact on prognosis. In a cohort of 894 breast cancer patients, FGFR1 amplification was present in 6.6% (33/503) of assessable tumors and was enriched in the luminal B-like subtype (69.7% of FGFR1-amplified tumors vs. 32.6% of non-amplified tumors). Due to the very low frequency of FGFR2 (<1%) and FGFR3 (<1%) amplifications, outcome analyses focused only on FGFR1 amplification.
The results showed that FGFR1 amplification was associated with a trend toward poorer outcomes, particularly shorter distant metastasis–free survival (DMFS; p=0.04, unadjusted analysis); however, this difference did not reach statistical significance in analysis adjusted for other well-known prognostic factors (P=0.05). No significant effect of FGFR1 amplification was observed on other secondary outcomes, including overall survival (OS) and local recurrence–free survival (LRFS).
These findings indicate that FGFR1 amplification is disproportionately associated with luminal B-like breast cancers (luminal B-like enriched), which are typically more aggressive and have higher proliferation rates. The absence of a statistically significant prognostic association in this study is likely due to the small number of FGFR1-amplified cases (n = 33), limiting statistical power.
name: EID12487

source.title: Impact of fibroblast growth factor receptor 1 (FGFR1) amplification on the prognosis of breast cancer patients.

description: In this 2005 study, immunohistochemical staining was used to assess the subcellular localization of NPM in 1,835 paraffin-embedded tumor specimens, including 591 from primary AML patients (ages 15–60), 135 from secondary AML patients, and 980 from hematopoietic and non-hematopoietic neoplasms other than AML. Of the 591 specimens tested, 208 (35.2%) were found to have aberrant cytoplasmic NPM localization (NPMc+), while the remainder displayed normal nuclear localization (NPMc–). Subsequent RT-PCR and Sanger sequencing found 51/52 NPMc+ specimens harbored a NPM1 exon 11 (NM_002520) mutation that results in a distinct C-terminal sequence and is predicted to alter the NPM protein at its C-terminus (referred to in this study as NPM exon 12 mutations). Transfection of NIH-3T3 cells with the NPM1 mutant alleles showed aberrant cytoplasmic localization compared to wild type, demonstrating a causal relationship between NPM1 mutation status and aberrant subcellular localization. NPMc+ was found to be associated with a normal karyotype in approximately 60% of AML patients (142/230, 61.7%). FLT3 internal tandem duplications were found to be twice as frequent in NPMc+ vs. NPMc- specimens, suggesting these mutations may be mechanistically linked. The majority of NPMc+ AML specimens were CD34- (49/52) and had a wide morphologic spectrum, demonstrating multilineage involvement. Finally, the authors investigated the response to induction therapy in 126 patients with AML and a normal karyotype (79 NPMc+, 47 NPMc-) treated according to the GIMEMA LAM99P protocol. AML patients with a normal karyotype and NPMc+ were found to have a relatively good response to induction chemotherapy. The study illustrates that AML cases characterized by NPM1 mutations represent a unique disease subtype with shared morphologic features, immunophenotype  and molecular and clinical characteristics.

disease.name: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With Mutated NPM1

name: EID12494

source.title: Cytoplasmic nucleophosmin in acute myelogenous leukemia with a normal karyotype.

description: In this 2005 study, the authors investigated the prevalence and prognostic impact of NPM1 mutation status in 300 adult patients with AML (16-60 years of age) with normal cytogenetics. The diagnostic bone marrow or peripheral blood sample of these 300 patients were analyzed and included the following: 257 patients with de novo AML, 24 patients with t-AML/s-AML, and 19 patients with no available information. NPM1 exon 11 mutations (referred to in this study as NPM exon 12 mutations) were identified in 145/300 (48%) of the specimens tested, representing the most frequent molecular event that has been identified in AML patients with a normal karyotype to-date. The majority of identified NPM1 mutations resulted in a 4 base pair insertion. Universally all mutations resulted in protein elongation and replacement of the last 7 amino acids in NPM1. Mutation status for FLT3, CEPBA, and MLL were also assessed. FLT3 internal tandem duplications (ITDs) and tyrosine kinase domain mutations (TKDs) were more frequently identified in the NPM1-mutated group (41% and 15% respectively) compared to the NPM1 negative group (25% and 5% respectively). NPM1-mutated/FLT3 ITD-negative mutation status was significantly associated with induction success and arose as a prognostic marker for achievement of complete remission (odds ratio = 2.81, 95% CI = 1.39-5.69). In addition, NPM1-mutated/FLT3 ITD-negative patients had significantly better relapse-free survival and overall survival.  In summary, NPM1 mutations were frequent in AML and were associated with specific clinical (favorable outcome) and genetic characteristics (normal cytogenetics and FLT3 mutations).

disease.name: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With Mutated NPM1

name: EID12495

source.title: Mutant nucleophosmin (NPM1) predicts favorable prognosis in younger adults with acute myeloid leukemia and normal cytogenetics: interaction with other gene mutations.

description: Amplification of FGFR1 is one molecular alteration associated with hormonal resistance and relapse in breast cancer. Using two different patient data cohorts (H12O - patients diagnosed at Hospital 12 de Octubre [n = 251] and METABRIC [n=98 patients]) with hormone-positive breast cancer (HRPBC), FISH studies demonstrated FGFR1 amplification in 11.8% of H12O patients. This was validated in the METABRIC cohort, where 7.6% of HRPBC demonstrated FGFR1 amplification. Furthermore, both studies found that FGFR1 amplification was more common in luminal B (16.3% H12O, 11.1% METABRIC) versus luminal A (6.6%, 5.5%) subtype. Using the H12O cohort, RNA expression analysis revealed 17% of cases had FGFR1 overexpression. Cumulatively, 24.5% of patients had altered FGFR1 expression as measured by FISH (amplification) and/or RNA expression (overexpression). From the H12O cohort, the median relapse-free survival time for patients with FGFR1-amplification was 9.3 years, which is significantly lower than the median relapse-free survival time for patients with non-FGFR1-amplified breast cancer (11.2 years). From the METABRIC cohort, the median relapse-free survival for patients with FGFR1-amplified breast cancer was 12.2 years, which is lower than patients without the FGFR1-amplication in which the median relapse-free survival was 21.1 years. The discrepancy between the median relapse-free survival rates between the cohorts, might be attributed to the demographic and clinical characteristics of the patients in each cohort, with the patients in the METABRIC being slightly older and having earlier stage breast cancer (T1/T2 and N0/N1 stages) than the H12O cohort. However, in both cohorts, when breast cancer was sub-classified by luminal type A or B, the difference in the relapse-free survival time between FGFR1-amplified and non-amplified was no longer significant. When median relapse-free survival included patients with FGFR1 amplification and/or FGFR1 overexpression, the average relapse free survival was 8.8 years for versus 11.2 from non-amplified/non-overexpressed. This analysis combining amplification and overexpression was not performed on the luminal subtypes. In conclusion, FGFR1 amplification is found in HRPBC, more often in the luminal B subtype, and is associated with worse prognosis in HRPBC, however the prognostic consequences of FGFR1 amplification are lost when HRPBC is classified by luminal subtypes.
name: EID12497

source.title: FGFR1 amplification or overexpression and hormonal resistance in luminal breast cancer: rationale for a triple blockade of ER, CDK4/6, and FGFR1.

description: In a clinical cohort of patients with HR+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer (n=110), FGFR1 amplification status was determined using FISH analysis (FGFR1/centromere 8 ratio ≥2). Among those receiving endocrine therapy alone, FGFR1 amplification (n=30) was associated with poorer outcomes based on time to progression (TTP) compared to those without FGFR1 amplification (n=80). FGFR1 amplification was not associated with a shorter TTP with chemotherapy, and the shorter TTP with endocrine therapy was not observed when combined with an mTOR inhibitor (everolimus). In patients treated with endocrine therapy and a CDK4/6 inhibitor, those with FGFR1 amplification had a shorter TTP, but the sample size was too small to determine statistical significance. A multivariate analysis supported FGFR1 as an independent predictive variable in shorter TTP with endocrine therapy alone but not when combined with mTOR inhibitors.
name: EID12498

source.title: FGFR1 Amplification Mediates Endocrine Resistance but Retains TORC Sensitivity in Metastatic Hormone Receptor-Positive (HR+) Breast Cancer.

description: To determine if there is a causal relationship between hormonal blockade (a frequent treatment for tumors in the adjuvant setting) and FGFR1 amplification/overexpression, this study used two non-FGFR1 amplified (MCF7 and T-47D) and one FGFR1 amplified (HCC1428) cell lines and exposed them to prolonged hormonal deprivation to mimic hormonal blockade treatment. After prolonged hormonal deprivation, all three cell lines developed estrogen-deprivation resistance as well as resistance to the selective estrogen receptor degrader, Fulvestrant, a therapy typically used upon metastatic relapse. The two cell lines that came from non-FGFR1 amplified parental lines had increased FGFR1 mRNA and protein levels after prolonged hormonal deprivation. However, engineered overexpression of FGFR1 in the non-FGFR1 amplified parental cell lines did not confer resistance to estrogen deprivation but did confer resistance to Fulvestrant. Furthermore adding Palbociclib, a CDK4/6 inhibitor frequently used in combination with Fulvestrant, all hormone-resistant FGFR1 amplified or overexpressed cell lines were resistant to the Fulvestrant + Palbociclib combination. However, this resistance was lost after adding Rogaratinib, a pan-FGFR inhibitor, to the Fulvestrant + Palbociclib combination, as shown by drastic growth reduction/no growth in culture, suggesting high sensitivity to this triple combination. To further understand mechanisms of resistance and sensitivity, the amount of Rb phosphorylation, CCND1 protein, and BrdU incorporation were measured in the various treatment conditions, due to their role in cell cycle progression. While fulvestrant or palbociclib result in some reduction in Rb phosphorylation, treatment with a doublet combination of fulvestrant + rogaratinib, or triple combination of Fulvestrant, Palbociclib, and Rogaratinib resulted in suppression of Rb phosphorylation and cell cycle arrest. This suggests that the triple blockade of ER, CDK4/6, and FGFR1 might be an appropriate therapy for FGFR1 altered, hormonal resistant breast cancer.
name: EID12503

source.title: FGFR1 amplification or overexpression and hormonal resistance in luminal breast cancer: rationale for a triple blockade of ER, CDK4/6, and FGFR1.

description: FGFR1 amplification (FGFR1amp) is frequently detected in metastatic breast cancer (MBC), where it is recognized as a generic marker of poor prognosis and most notably, resistance to CDK4/6 inhibitors and endocrine therapy. This prompted development of multityrosine kinase inhibitors (MTKIs) and pan-selective FGFR inhibitors (FGFRis) to treat specifically FGFR1-altered breast cancer; however, not all patients with FGFR1amp responded to FGFRis, leading to the hypothesis that FGFR mRNA expression may be a more accurate predictor of treatment response than gene copy number alterations (CNAs). In addition, up to 30% of breast cancers reveal concurrent amplification of FGFR1 and amplification of 11q13 segment encompassing cyclin D1 (CCND1) and 3 FGF ligands (FGFR3/4/19). Thus, 17 breast cancer patient-derived xenografts (PDXs) harboring amplifications in FGFR1 or 4 and/or 11q13 amplification (7 PDXs and FGFR1amp without 11q13amp, 4 PDXs with co-amplification of FGFR1 and 11q13, 3 PDXs with FGFR4amp, and 3 PDXs with 11q13amp), and samples from 10 patients treated with either FGFRis or MTKIs, were evaluated for antitumor activity. FFPE tumor samples were used for mRNA levels measurement (using nCounter and HTG EdgeSeq methods), and treatment effects on proliferation and angiogenesis were assessed by immunofluorescence detection of Ki-67 and CD31. High FGFR1–4 mRNA expression, rather than CNAs, was a more accurate biomarker for FGFRi sensitivity, with responders showing MAPK pathway downregulation. Rogaratinib, a pan-FGFR1–4 inhibitor, achieved partial or stable responses in 53% of models, while lucitanib, an MTKI, showed superior efficacy (86%) across FGFRi-resistant and FGFR-independent models due to its dual antiproliferative and antiangiogenic effects. Amplification of the 11q13 locus, which includes FGF3/4/19 and CCND1, frequently co-occurred with FGFR1amp and enhanced FGFRi sensitivity, especially when FGF ligands were overexpressed. A composite biomarker based on FGFR1–4 mRNA levels predicted treatment response with high accuracy (ROC AUC = 0.94), and in a cohort of 339 breast cancer samples, FGFR1 CNA was frequent but only moderately correlated with mRNA expression. Attempts to mimic lucitanib’s dual mechanism by combining rogaratinib with anti-VEGF agents showed limited efficacy, underscoring the therapeutic advantage of MTKIs like lucitanib in FGFR-addicted and resistant breast cancers. In conclusion, FGFR inhibitors may offer effective treatment for metastatic breast cancer patients with high FGFR1–4 mRNA expression, especially those resistant to CDK4/6 inhibitors or lacking targeted options in triple-negative breast cancer, but this approach requires further clinical validation.
name: EID12505

source.title: High FGFR1-4 mRNA Expression Levels Correlate with Response to Selective FGFR Inhibitors in Breast Cancer.

description: In a phase II trial of 49 NSCLC patients with STK11 mutation, the MTORC1/2 inhibitor vistusertib did not result in any responses.
name: EID12514

source.title: A phase II trial of mTORC1/2 inhibition in STK11 deficient non small cell lung cancer.

description: Preclinical studies demonstrated that the LSD1 inhibitor HCI-2509 reduced proliferation and induced apoptosis in five EWSR1-FLI1 fusion-positive Ewing sarcoma cell lines (A673, TC32, TC71, SK-N-MC, CHLA-10) compared to DMSO controls (p < 0.05), whereas non-Ewing sarcoma lines were relatively resistant. In A673 cells, fusion dependence was confirmed as EWSR1-FLI1 fusion (EWS/FLI) knockdown reduced drug sensitivity (EC50 113nM, 95% CI 81.9 - 158nM, 95% CI 1,111 - 2,999). In xenograft models derived from A673, TC71, and SK-N-MC cells (n = 8-10 per arm), daily HCI-2509 treatment significantly delayed tumor growth compared with vehicle (two-way ANOVA P<0.0001) and improved survival (log-rank P<0.05), with histologic evidence of reduced Ki-67 and increased cleaved caspase-3.
name: EID12516

source.title: Reversible LSD1 inhibition interferes with global EWS/ETS transcriptional activity and impedes Ewing sarcoma tumor growth.

description: In this 2017 study the author included 44 cellular myofibroblastic tumors previously diagnosed as cellular myofibroma, cellular myopericytoma, or cellular myofibroblastic neoplasms (NOS), and a control group of 34 various myofibroblastic lesions, including typical myofibromas (adult and infantile variants), myopericytomas, malignant myopericytomas, low grade myofibroblastic sarcomas, and myofibroblastomas. RT-PCR and FISH was utilised to investigate SRF gene abnormalities. SRF gene rearrangements were detected in 10 cases of cellular myofibroblastic tumors and not detected in any of the control group, including classic examples of both myofibroma and myopericytoma. SRF::RELA fusions were present in 7 tumours, while another case had a SRF::C3orf62 fusion and in two cases the partner was not identified. RT-PCR confirmed fusion of SRF exon 4 with RELA exon 11 in one case. The cohort was composed of 7 females and 3 males, with a wide age range at diagnosis, of 3 months to 63 years (mean 17; median 14), the majority under the age of 18 years. The anatomic distribution was quite broad. The authors concluded that they have identified a subset of cellular myofibroblastic tumors occurring mostly in children and young adults, with morphologic features in keeping with cellular variants of myofibroma and myopericytoma, and harboring recurrent gene rearrangements in the SRF gene which in the majority of these cases resulted in SRF::RELA gene fusions.
name: EID12517

source.title: Recurrent SRF-RELA Fusions Define a Novel Subset of Cellular Myofibroma/Myopericytoma: A Potential Diagnostic Pitfall With Sarcomas With Myogenic Differentiation.

description: In this 2020 study, the authors include 13 perivascular myoid tumors belonging to the previously described SRF rearranged subtype of tumors (PMID:28248815), which share morphologic features with myopericytomas and myofibromas and express smooth muscle markers similarly to most perivascular myoid tumors. The cohort was composed of 6 males and 7 females, and all patients except 1 were pediatric, with a mean age of 11.8 years (ranging from 1  week to 73  years). RNA-sequencing was successfully performed on 12 samples and detected the SRF::RELA fusion in 6 tumors, SRF::NCOA2 in 3 tumors, while SRF::CITED1, SRF::NFKBIE, and CITED2::SRF were detected once. The breakpoints were located in exons (ENST00000265354) 2 to 5 of the SRF gene. The tumors occurred in different anatomic sites, although often tumors (n=8) were situated in the head. Follow-up data showed that tumors seem to be nonaggressive. The authors concluded that they have expanded the molecular spectrum of the perivascular tumors with SRF rearrangement by identifying 4 additional fusion genes and suggest naming the distinct clinicopathologic entity SRF-fused perivascular tumor.
name: EID12518

source.title: SRF Fusions Other Than With RELA Expand the Molecular Definition of SRF-fused Perivascular Tumors.

description: In this 2023 study, the authors included 3 cases of SRF rearranged cellular myofibromas/perivascular myoid tumors diagnosed in children, aged 7 to 16 years. RNA sequencing was utilized to detect SRF::NCOA3, SRF::RELA, and SRF::NFKBIE gene fusions in the 3 tumors. All 3 cases occurred in the extremities. The authors concluded that they have described 3 cases of rare SRF rearranged cellular myofibromas/perivascular myoid tumors with a smooth muscle-like phenotype in children and expanded the molecular spectrum by identifying a new fusion gene, NCOA3.
name: EID12519

source.title: Cellular myofibromas with SRF fusions: clinicopathological and molecular study of 3 cases of a rare entity and a potential mimic of sarcoma.

description: In this 2024 case report, the authors included 2 cases of SRF rearranged cellular perivascular myoid tumors diagnosed in a 3-month-old male and a 3-year-old female. FISH and next-generation sequencing were utilised to detect an SRF::NCOA2 gene fusion in case 1 and a SRF::RELA gene fusion in case 2, respectively. The authors conclude that SRF rearranged cellular perivascular myoid tumors have a broad morphologic spectrum ranging from a pericytic pattern to a myoid pattern, and include hybrid tumors with a mixture of pericytic and myoid patterns, and can be misdiagnosed as myogenic sarcomas.
name: EID12520

source.title: [SRF-rearranged cellular perivascular myoid tumor: a clinicopathological analysis of two cases].

description:
In this Swedish population-based study, the authors retrospectively re-evaluated 71 poorly differentiated supratentorial CNS tumors in children, previously diagnosed as CNS-PNETs, to assess their molecular features, including BCOR genetic alterations. The cohort included 39 males and 32 females, with a median age at diagnosis of 6.2 years. Using WHO 2021 histopathological guidelines and the Molecular Neuropathology (MNP) brain tumor classifier, 10% (n=7) of tumors were subclassified as CNS neuroblastoma with FOXR2 activation (CNS NB-FOXR2). All seven CNS NB-FOXR2 tumors showed complete concordance between histology-based diagnoses and DNA methylation-based classification, with a calibrated score (CS) ≥ 0.9.
The median age at diagnosis of CNS NB-FOXR2 patients was 5.3 years (range 2.5–15.7), with 43% males (n=3) and 57% females (n=4). Copy number analysis predicted gain of chromosome 1q in all seven tumors, and whole or partial loss of chromosome 16q in 86% (6/7) of cases. While the overall CNS-PNET cohort demonstrated poor outcomes (5-year PFS 38% ±11%, 5-year OS 45% ±12%), CNS NB-FOXR2 patients had excellent prognosis, with both 5-year PFS and OS at 100%.
These findings highlight that CNS NB-FOXR2 represents a rare, molecularly distinct entity within pediatric CNS-PNETs, and that DNA methylation profiling provides a reliable diagnostic tool to accurately identify this tumor type, which is associated with favorable long-term outcomes.
name: EID12521

source.title: Supratentorial CNS-PNETs in children; a Swedish population-based study with molecular re-evaluation and long-term follow-up.

description: Phase II trial (NCT04484142) of Dato-DXd 6 mg/kg every 3 weeks in 137 heavily pretreated patients with advanced NSCLC harboring actionable genomic alterations (57% EGFR-mutant; 51% with prior brain metastases). The confirmed ORR was 35.8% (95% CI 27.8–44.4) with a median DOR of 7.0 months. In subgroup analyses, ORR was 43.6% (95% CI 32.9-54.8) in EGFR-mutant patients and 23.5% in those with ALK rearrangements, with corresponding median PFS of 5.8 and 4.3 months. All four complete responses occurred in patients with EGFR mutations. Grade ≥ 3 TRAEs occurred in 28.5% of patients, most commonly stomatitis (9.5%), with oral mucositis and anemia as notable AESIs.
name: EID12522

source.title: Datopotamab Deruxtecan in Advanced or Metastatic Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer With Actionable Genomic Alterations: Results From the Phase II TROPION-Lung05 Study.

description: TROPION-Lung01 (NCT04656652) was a global, randomized, open-label phase III trial of 604 patients with previously treated advanced NSCLC comparing datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd) with docetaxel. Dato-DXd significantly improved progression-free survival (4.4 vs 3.7 months; HR 0.75; P = 0.004) but not overall survival (12.9 vs 11.8 months; HR 0.94; P = 0.530), with greater benefit in nonsquamous disease (PFS HR 0.63; OS HR 0.84) and a higher objective response rate (26.4% vs 12.8%). Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events were less frequent with Dato-DXd (25.6% vs 42.1%), with stomatitis and interstitial lung disease (ILD) as notable adverse events of special interest (AESIs).
name: EID12523

source.title: Datopotamab Deruxtecan Versus Docetaxel for Previously Treated Advanced or Metastatic Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: The Randomized, Open-Label Phase III TROPION-Lung01 Study.

description:
In this 2016 study, the authors analyzed 398 newly diagnosed Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML) patients, identifying 12 (3%) cases that lacked the Philadelphia (Ph) chromosome by conventional cytogenetic analysis but were positive for the BCR::ABL1 fusion by RT-PCR. Six Ph– cases were further characterized to investigate the cytogenetic mechanisms responsible for this rearrangement. FISH analysis revealed cryptic insertions between chromosomes 9 and 22 in five patients and a classic two-step translocation in one patient, demonstrating four distinct fusion signal patterns and highlighting significant genetic heterogeneity among Ph– CML cases.
The study found that the BCR::ABL1 fusion most frequently localized to chromosome 9q34 rather than the typical 22q11.2 region, contrasting with prior reports. These findings established that even in the absence of the visible Philadelphia chromosome, the presence of the BCR::ABL1 fusion gene serves as a definitive diagnostic hallmark of CML. The authors concluded that detection of BCR::ABL1 by FISH or molecular analysis is essential for confirming the diagnosis of CML in patients with a normal karyotype, supporting its role as the primary molecular event defining the disease.
name: EID12526

source.title: Cryptic BCR-ABL fusion gene as variant rearrangement in chronic myeloid leukemia: molecular cytogenetic characterization and influence on TKIs therapy.

description: The authors report evaluation of zongertinib in a multicohort, phase 1a/1b trial involving patients with advanced or metastatic HER2-mutant non-small cell lung cancer. Three cohorts of patients are reported. The cohorts differed in the type of ERBB2 mutation present, prior treatment, and in the treatment dose/timing with zongertinib.  In cohort 1 (n=75), patients had a mutation in the tyrosine kinase domain of ERBB2, received zongertinib at a dose of 120 mg, and were NOT previously treated with a HER2-directed antibody-drug conjugate.  71% of these patients (95% [CI], 60 to 80; P<0.001 against a ≤30% benchmark) had a confirmed objective response. The median duration of response was 14.1 months (95% CI, 6.9 to not evaluable). The median progression-free survival was 12.4 months (95% CI, 8.2 to not evaluable).
name: EID12530

source.title: Zongertinib in Previously Treated HER2-Mutant Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer.

description:
The phase III INAVO120 trial (NCT04191499) in 325 patients with endocrine-resistant, PIK3CA-mutated HR⁺/HER2⁻ locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer evaluated inavolisib plus palbociclib and fulvestrant (n=161) versus placebo plus palbociclib and fulvestrant (n=164). Median PFS was 15.0 months (95% CI 11.3–20.5) versus 7.3 months (95% CI 5.6–9.3; HR 0.43; 95% CI 0.32–0.59; P<.0001), with ORR of 58% (95% CI 50–66) and median DOR of 18.4 months compared to 25% (95% CI 19–32) and 9.6 months in the control arm. The most common adverse events (≥20%) included neutropenia, hyperglycemia, stomatitis, diarrhea, and rash, consistent with the PI3Kα inhibitor class. 
Efficacy outcomes were reported for all eligible PIK3CA mutations detected by the FoundationOne Liquid CDx assay, which covers hotspot mutations in exons 2 (R88, G106, K111, G118), 5 (N345), 8 (C420, E453), 10 (E542, E545, Q546), and 21 (M1043, H1047, G1049); individual patient numbers by mutation were not provided.

description: The phase 2 FIGHT-207 basket study was designed to evaluate pemigatinib, a selective FGFR inhibitor, in patients with previously treated advanced solid tumors harboring FGFR alterations. Eligible patients were ≥18 years old with a histologically or cytologically confirmed advanced/metastatic or surgically unresectable solid tumor and radiographically measurable disease per RECIST v.1.1 or RANO criteria. Safety was consistent with previous reports. This study consisted of three cohorts defined by FGFR alteration category. Patients with in-frame FGFR1–FGFR3 fusions and rearrangements, including intact kinase domains, were assigned to cohort A (n=49). Cohort B (n=32) consisted of patients with FGFR actionable single-nucleotide variants (SNVs), excluding kinase domain SNVs, considered known or likely to be activating and actionable. This set included specific somatic missense mutations, insertions or deletions of FGFR1–FGFR3 that were known or likely activating. Cohort C (n=26) included the remaining patients with FGFR1–FGFR3 mutations in the kinase domain or FGFR1–3 VUS with potential pathogenicity. Most patients underwent local testing with the FoundationOne CDx assay (Foundation Medicine), which profiles 324 genes at high coverage (>500×), with some tested using alternative platforms. Six Breast Cancer patients were included in this study: One in cohort B and five in cohort C. FGFR amplification, defined as a copy number ≥6, was identified in nine patients. These included cases with concurrent FGFR mutations or fusions, as well as amplifications in alternative FGFR genes unrelated to the primary alteration. FGFR1 amplification was observed in five patients, including two breast cancer cases in cohort C. Exploratory endpoints included objective response rate (ORR) of cohort C and analysis of co-alterations associated with resistance and response. ORRs for cohorts A, B and C were 26.5% (13/49), 9.4% (3/32) and 3.8% (1/26), respectively. Although new therapeutic areas for FGFR inhibition and mechanisms of drug failure were identified across tumor types, the FIGHT-207 study was terminated early by the sponsor for business reasons. As a result, some tumor and molecular cohorts were underpowered, limiting the ability to draw definitive conclusions about FGFR dependency for specific alterations. Additionally, the small number of patients with concurrent FGFR gene amplification precluded evaluation of its potential impact on pemigatinib response.
name: EID12542

source.title: Pemigatinib in previously treated solid tumors with activating FGFR1-FGFR3 alterations: phase 2 FIGHT-207 basket trial.

description: In a sub-analysis of a randomized phase II trial in extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma (EWSR1-NR4A3 and TAF15-NR4A3 fusions; n = 2) and mesenchymal chondrosarcoma (HEY1-NCOA2 fusion, n = 6)(trabectedin n = 5; BSC n = 3), the two EMCS patients treated with trabectedin 1.2 mg/m² q3w achieved stable disease with PFS 13.0 and 7.4 mo and OS 26.4 and 10.4 mo. Tumor shrinkage of 1% and 27 % was observed; both eventually progressed. Whereas the three MCS patients in the BSC arm all had PD (median PFS 1.0 mo, 95 % CI 0.3–1.0). No ≥ G4 or fatal AEs occurred.
name: EID12545

source.title: Results of sub-analysis of a phase 2 study on trabectedin treatment for extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma and mesenchymal chondrosarcoma.

description: In retrospective analyses of two large ICI-treated solid tumor cohorts (DFCI n = 789, MSKCC n = 1250), CDKN2A loss-of-function alterations were associated with significantly worse overall survival and shorter time-to-treatment failure in urothelial carcinoma (UC DFCI n = 109, UC MSKCC n = 206). In the DCFI cohort, median OS was 8.8 vs 25.2 months (HR 1.8, 95% CI 1.1–3.1; p = 0.019) and median TTF 4.2 vs 8.4 months (HR 2.0, 95% CI 1.3–3.1; p = 0.002), while in the MSKCC cohort median OS was 11 vs 19 months (HR 1.7; 95% CI 1.1–2.6; p = 0.017). These results support CDKN2A loss as a predictive marker of resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors.
name: EID12546

source.title: CDKN2A Alterations and Response to Immunotherapy in Solid Tumors.

description:
Futibatinib is a selective FGFR inhibitor. In this 2020 preclinical study, its antitumor activity was evaluated in cancer cell lines and xenograft models. The antiproliferative activity was  assessed in cancer cell lines derived from various tissue origins, including the MFM-223 and MDA-MB-134-VI breast cancer cell lines, with or without FGFR genomic aberrations (amplifications, point mutations, fusions, or translocations), by measuring cell growth after three days of futibatinib exposure. Additionally, the antitumor activity of futibatinib was investigated in murine and rat xenograft models bearing tumors with FGFR genomic alterations. Mice received oral doses of futibatinib once daily for two weeks. Futibatinib demonstrated antiproliferative activity against the FGFR-deregulated MFM-223 breast cancer cell line, which harbors FGFR1/2 amplifications. Furthermore, robust tumor growth inhibition was observed in the FGFR1/2-amplified MFM-223 breast cancer xenograft model at daily doses ranging from 12.5 to 50 mg/kg.
In summary, the results of this study demonstrate that futibatinib is a potent, irreversible, and highly selective inhibitor of FGFR1–4, exhibiting broad antiproliferative activity in FGFR-deregulated cancer cell lines and animal tumor models.
name: EID12547

source.title: Futibatinib Is a Novel Irreversible FGFR 1-4 Inhibitor That Shows Selective Antitumor Activity against FGFR-Deregulated Tumors.

description: In a preclinical study using STK11/LKB1-deficient pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) cell lines (TB 32047, PANC-1, SUIT2, SU86.86, KPC792) and C57BL/6 orthotopic mouse models (n = 5 per group), the PDE4 inhibitor roflumilast (50 μM in vitro; 5 mg/kg/day in vivo) significantly reduced migration (p < 0.05 - 0.001) and tumor weight in STK11 knockout PDAC models compared with vehicle, without affecting cell viability. Loss of STK11 increased expression of PDE4D, PDE4B, and PDE10A, and roflumilast reversed pro-migratory/angiogenic gene signatures. Treatment was well tolerated with no observed toxicity.
name: EID12555

source.title: Roflumilast inhibits tumor growth and migration in STK11/LKB1 deficient pancreatic cancer.

description: In a cell line screen using MCF-7, exogenous expression of FGFR1 confers resistance to fulvestrant and fulvestrant plus ribociclib. In a study using breast cancer cell lines MCF-7 and T47D, overexpression of FGFR1 was found to confer resistance to fulvestrant plus ribociclib. Conversely, inhibition of FGFR signaling in three estrogen-receptor positive breast cancer cell lines with FGFR1 amplification restores sensitivity to fulvestrant/palbociclib combination. Growth of patient derived xenograft models harbouring FGFR1 amplification can be suppressed by the combination of FGFR inhibitor, fulvestrant and palbociclib. These observations are consistent with those of the MONALEESA cohort, where amplification or mRNA overexpression of FGFR1 is associated with shorter PFS when treated with CDK4/6 inhibitor, suggesting that FGFR1 amplification or overexpression is a mechanism of resistance to the combination treatment of fulvestrant and CDK4/6 inhibitor.
name: EID12557

source.title: Aberrant FGFR signaling mediates resistance to CDK4/6 inhibitors in ER+ breast cancer.

description: In a retrospective study of stage IV NSCLC patients treated with first-line platinum doublet chemotherapy (n = 103; 51 KEAP1/NFE2L2/CUL3-mutant, 52 WT), mutations in NFE2L2, KEAP1, or CUL3 were associated with significantly shorter time to treatment failure (2.8 vs 8.3 months; HR 2.19, 95% CI 1.42–3.38; p = 0.00036) and overall survival (11.2 vs 36.8 months; HR 2.17, 95% CI 1.34–3.52; p = 0.0016) compared with matched controls. In KRAS wild-type cases, OS (11.2 vs 38.1 months; p = 0.0039) and time on treatment (2.6 vs 8.5 months, p = 0.0001) remained shorter when compared to WT patients. Preclinical Keap1-deleted Trp53-based LUAD and LSCC mouse models lacking Kras mutations demonstrated increased clonogenic survival after exposure to cisplatin, carboplatin, paclitaxel, and etoposide, confirming that Keap1 loss drives intrinsic chemoresistance through NRF2 pathway activation.

molecularProfile.name: NFE2L2 Mutation OR KEAP1 Mutation OR CUL3 Mutation

name: EID12558

source.title: Role of KEAP1/NFE2L2 Mutations in the Chemotherapeutic Response of Patients with Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.

description: In preclinical pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) models with high NQ01 expression, which indicates the NFE2L2 (NRF2) pathway activation, the small molecule NSC84167 (NSLC01, 50 mg/kg) selectively inhibited tumor growth (p < 0.01, n = 7-8) and induced apoptosis in NRF2-high but not in NRF2-low PDXs. Across conventional and patient-derived PDAC cell lines, NSLC01 sensitivity correlated with NQO1 expression (r = −0.5563, p = 0.021), and NRF2 knockdown reversed drug sensitivity.
name: EID12560

source.title: Compound NSC84167 selectively targets NRF2-activated pancreatic cancer by inhibiting asparagine synthesis pathway.

description: In the phase III randomized open-label CheckMate 8HW trial (NCT04008030; n = 303, 255 centrally confirmed MSI-H/dMMR metastatic colorectal cancer), nivolumab plus ipilimumab significantly improved progression-free survival versus investigator’s choice of chemotherapy (mFOLFOX6 or FOLFIRI with or without bevacizumab or cetuximab) as first-line treatment (24-month PFS 72%, 95% CI 64–79 vs 14%, 95% CI 6–25; p < 0.001). The restricted mean survival time at 24 months was 10.6 months longer (95% CI 8.4–12.9) with nivolumab plus ipilimumab, and grade 3–4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 23% vs 48% of patients, respectively.

source.title: Nivolumab plus Ipilimumab in Microsatellite-Instability-High Metastatic Colorectal Cancer.

description: In the phase III randomized open-label CheckMate 8HW trial (NCT04008030; n = 707 randomized; centrally confirmed MSI-H/dMMR: n = 296 nivolumab+ipilimumab vs 286 nivolumab) showed nivolumab plus ipilimumab significantly improved progression-free survival versus nivolumab monotherapy across all treatment lines (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.48–0.81; p = 0.0003). Median PFS was not reached (95% CI 53.8-NE) with nivolumab plus ipilimumab and 39.3 months (22.1-NE) with nivolumab. Objective response rate was 71% (95% CI 65–76) vs 58% (95% CI 52–64; p = 0.0011), with complete responses in 30% and 28%, respectively. Grade ≥3 AEs occurred in 22% vs 14%, including diarrhea/colitis (3%), hypophysitis (3%), and adrenal insufficiency (3%), with three treatment-related deaths reported (2 myocarditis/pneumonitis in combination arm, 1 pneumonitis in monotherapy arm).

description: In the multicohort phase 1b Beamion LUNG-1 trial (NCT04886804) of zongertinib in HER2-mutant NSCLC, three cohorts were evaluated by mutation type and prior therapy. In cohort 1 (n = 75; HER2-TKD mutations, no prior HER2-ADC), the confirmed ORR was 71% (95% CI 60-80; P < 0.001), with median duration of response 14.1 months (95% CI 6.9-NE) and mPFS 12.4 months (95% CI 8.2-NE). Responses occurred across subtypes, including A775_G776insYVMA 81% (95 % CI 68-90); P780_Y781insGSP 75% (95% CI 41-93); other mutations 42% (95% CI 23-64). AEs included diarrhea (56%) and rash (33%) with grade ≥3 drug-related adverse events occurring in 17% (Alanine aminotransferase 8%, Aspartate aminotransferase 5%), and no treatment-related interstitial lung disease was reported.

description: In this 2017 study reviewing 753 sarcoma cases, 11 tumors with the BCOR::CCNB3 fusion were identified using immunohistochemistry and RT-PCR. These tumors were found exclusively in males, with a mean age of 12.9 years, and were predominantly located in the axial skeleton. Morphologically, the tumors showed spindled or round cells, vesicular nuclei, fine chromatin, inconspicuous nucleoli, and a characteristic arciform vascular pattern. Over 50% stained positive for SATB2 and Pax8, suggesting potential diagnostic value for these markers in identifying BCOR::CCNB3 positive sarcomas.

description: In the phase II trial (NCT02992743) of letetresgene autoleucel (lete-cel) in human leukocyte antigen ((HLA)-A*02:01–, HLA-A*02:05–, and/or HLA-A*02:06–positive), NY-ESO-1 (CTAG1B)-expressing advanced or metastatic myxoid/round cell liposarcoma (n = 20 treated), ORR was 20% (95% CI 2.5-55.6) with reduced-dose lymphodepletion and 40% (95% CI 12.2-73.8) with standard-dose lymphodepletion; median PFS was 5.4 months (95% CI 2.0-11.5) and 8.7 months (95% CI 0.9-NE), respectively. Grade ≥3 cytokine release syndrome occurred in 10% and 30% of patients, and all events resolved. These results support the activity of lete-cel for HLA-/NY-ESO-1-positive MRCLS.

description:
Microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) colorectal cancers (CRC) respond to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICPIs), but response rates vary, often < 50%, highlighting the need for better stratification.  This retrospective study evaluated tumor mutational burden (TMB) as a predictive biomarker in 22 MSI-H mCRC patients treated with PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors, including 19 on pembrolizumab.
Among these patients, ORR was 68% (15/22), with 7 complete and 8 partial responses. TMB was strongly associated with ORR and PFS in both univariate (P < 0.001) and multivariate (P < 0.01) analyses.  Log-rank analysis identified the optimal TMB cut-point between 37 and 41 mutations/Mb. All patients with TMB ≥37 responded; most (6 of 9 ) with lower TMB progressed. Median PFS was not reached in the TMB-high group (median follow-up >18 months), while it was 2 months in the TMB-low group. 
Validation in a larger cohort of 18,140 CRC cases (821/4.5% MSI-H) confirmed the cut-point (37.4 mutations/Mb), corresponding to the 35th percentile. Patients below this threshold were less likely to benefit from PD-1/PD-L1 monotherapy. 
TMB was measured from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue using a hybrid capture-based NGS assay (Foundation Medicine), targeting 315–324 cancer-related genes across a 0.8–1.2 Mb genomic region. The assay used somatic-only sequencing with computational germline filtering. TMB calculations included both synonymous and non-synonymous variants and were validated against whole exome sequencing (WES), ensuring methodological accuracy. 
These findings support integrating TMB into clinical workflows and highlight the need for prospective validation in larger cohorts.
name: EID12574

source.title: Tumor mutational burden is predictive of response to immune checkpoint inhibitors in MSI-high metastatic colorectal cancer.

description: In non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) models, KEAP1-mutant cell lines (H838, H460) exhibited strong sensitivity to NSC84167 (NSLC01) in MTT cell viability assays, with IC₅₀ values well below 1 µM, which is considerably lower than the 3 µM cutoff for sensitivity. In contrast, KEAP1-wild-type cells (HCC193, H1299) were resistant. This pattern suggests that loss of KEAP1 and subsequent NRF2 pathway activation predict a response to NSLC01.
name: EID12575

source.title: Compound NSC84167 selectively targets NRF2-activated pancreatic cancer by inhibiting asparagine synthesis pathway.

description:
This retrospective study examined the association between TMB and clinical response to immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) across multiple cancer types. 

1,662 advanced cancer patients treated with at least one dose of ICI, including avelumab, durvalumab, ipilimumab, nivolumab, pembrolizumab or tremelimumab as monotherapy or in combination (146 received anti-CTLA-4, 1,256 received anti-PD-1 or PD-L1, and 260 received the combination), were included in the study. Tumour-derived and matched normal germline DNA were sequenced using the MSK-IMPACT targeted 468-cancer gene panel. TMB was calculated as the number of somatic nonsynonymous per megabase sequences. 

Using top 20% within each cancer type as the cutoff, a significant association of improved overall survival with higher TMB was observed in patients with bladder (n=214, p=0.040), colorectal (n=110, p= 0.031), head and neck (n=138, p=7.42 × 10e-3), and non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) (n=350, p= 2.30× 10e-4), and across the whole cohort (n=1,662, p= 1.59 × 10e-6). A similar trend was also observed in breast cancer (n=45), esophagogastric cancer (n=126), melanoma (n=321), renal cell carcinoma (n=151), and cancer of unknown primary (n=90), despite not reaching statistical significance. This association was also observed using different cut points ranging between top10-50% to define high TMB. Similarly, improved clinical benefit/ progression free survival were also associated higher TMB among patients with NSCLC, melanoma, esophagogastric, head and neck, and renal cell carcinoma. Notably, distinct from these cancer types, no association between higher TMB and improved patient survival was observed in glioma (n=117). 

A cohort of 5,371 advanced cancer patients who did not receive ICI were also included in this study. A lack of prognostic benefit of TMB status was observed both across the cancer types and within each histology, demonstrating the observed survival difference among patients with TMB high tumours was attributed to ICI treatment. 

The authors also noted that stratifying by TMB decile within histology was chosen in this study to demonstrate the relationship between TMB and patient prognosis, although this method may not be ideal for clinical use.

Overall, this study demonstrated the clinical value of higher TMB in predicting superior overall survival in patients across multiple cancer types. However, the authors also noted that stratifying by TMB decile within histology was chosen in this study to demonstrate the relationship between TMB and patient prognosis, although this method may not be ideal for clinical use.
name: EID12578

source.title: Tumor mutational load predicts survival after immunotherapy across multiple cancer types.

description: In a sub-analysis of a randomized phase II trial in extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma (EWSR1-NR4A3 and TAF15-NR4A3 fusions) and mesenchymal chondrosarcoma (HEY1-NCOA2 fusion)(trabectedin n = 5; BSC n = 3), the three MCS patients treated with trabectedin 1.2 mg/m² q3w achieved PFS 22.2, 7.5, and 12.5 mo with a 6-month progression-free rate of 100% and best responses of 1 partial response (PR) of -58% and 2 stable disease (SD) of 1% and -1% (no progressive disease (PD)).  Whereas, three MCS patients in the BSC arm all had PD (median PFS 1.0 mo, 95 % CI 0.3-1.0). No ≥ G4 or fatal AEs occurred.
name: EID12585

source.title: Results of sub-analysis of a phase 2 study on trabectedin treatment for extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma and mesenchymal chondrosarcoma.

description: High Tumor Mutation Burden (TMB >19 mutations/Mb) represents a robust and platform-validated genomic biomarker predictive of clinical benefit from PD-1/PD-L1 immune checkpoint blockade in non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). This threshold was derived through regression tree modeling across multiple sequencing platforms (MSK-IMPACT, DFCI-OncoPanel, and whole-exome sequencing) and validated in three large, independent cohorts totaling 1,552 patients. Patients with high TMB demonstrated significantly improved objective response rate (49.1% vs 21.5%, p<0.001), progression-free survival (11.4 vs 2.8 months, p<0.001), and overall survival (36.1 vs 12.4 months, p<0.001) compared with those with low TMB, independent of PD-L1 expression levels. Molecular and immune profiling revealed that high-TMB NSCLCs exhibit enhanced CD8⁺ and PD-1⁺ T-cell infiltration, increased PD-L1 expression, and activation of antigen presentation pathways. The authors suggested that TMB >19 mut/Mb is a clinically actionable biomarker for identifying NSCLC patients most likely to respond to PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors.
name: EID12586

source.title: Association of High Tumor Mutation Burden in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancers With Increased Immune Infiltration and Improved Clinical Outcomes of PD-L1 Blockade Across PD-L1 Expression Levels.

description: This retrospective study evaluated the clinical utility of blood tumour mutational burden (bTMB) as a predictive biomarker for atezolizumab efficacy in advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) who had progressed from first-line therapy using samples collected prospectively from 2 randomized trials. The cfDNA assay used in this study utilised the same 1.1 Mb tissue FoundationOne hybridization capture panel (394 genes). The bTMB score was calculated by identifying all base substitutions present at an allele frequency of ≥0.5%, with predicted germline variants filtered out. Pre-treatment plasma bTMB demonstrated a positive correlation with the patient-paired tissue TMB (tTMB) (Spearman rank correlation = 0.64, n=259). Based on this correlation, an optimal cut-off point of ≥ 16 mutations per megabase (with a minimum somatic allele frequency ≥ 1%) was selected for subsequent clinical evaluation. Applying the cut off of bTMB ≥ 16 mutations per megabase to the POPLAR study (NCT01903993) (n=211) demonstrated improved progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) benefit with atezolizumab versus docetaxel. At this cut-off, the PFS hazard ratio (HR) was 0.57. The median PFS was 4.2 months in the atezolizumab arm and 2.9 months in the docetaxel arm; the median OS values were 13.0 and 7.4 months, respectively. The biomarker-treatment interaction for PFS at bTMB ≥ 16 trended towards significance (interaction P = 0.055). The predictive value was independently validated in the larger OAK study (NCT02008227) (n=583). Patients bTMB ≥16 muts/Mb showed significant PFS benefit from atezolizumab (HR: 0.65, P=0.013), with the biomarker-treatment interaction for PFS being statistically significant (P=0.036). Although the OS benefit in this subgroup was substantial (median 13.5 versus 6.8 months, HR: 0.64), the treatment interaction for overall survival was not significant. The findings support bTMB ≥16 mutations per megabase as a non-invasive biomarker for predicting enhanced PFS benefit from atezolizumab in advanced NSCLC patients who have progressed on first-line therapy.
name: EID12587

source.title: Blood-based tumor mutational burden as a predictor of clinical benefit in non-small-cell lung cancer patients treated with atezolizumab.

description: This retrospective analysis assessed the association between tumor mutational burden (TMB) and the efficacy of nivolumab plus low-dose ipilimumab as first-line treatment for advanced/metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in the CheckMate 568 trial (NCT02477826). The TMB was calculated using the FoundationOne CDx assay, which covers 324 genes. TMB was defined as the number of somatic, coding, base substitutions, and short indels per Mb of genome examined, with predicted germline variants excluded from the calculation. Of the 139 patients enrolled, 98 had successful TMB results, where 49% of patients had high-TMB (defined as ≥ 10 mut/Mb). The overall response rate (ORR) was 44% in the high-TMB group versus 12% in the low-TMB group. The association of efficacy with TMB was independent of tumor PD-L1 expression status. TMB was shown to be an informative classifier for ORR (AUC= 0.73; 95% CI, 0.62-0.84). Median progression-free survival (PFS) was also longer in patients with high-TMB compared to those with low-TMB (7.1 months [95% CI, 3.6 to 11.3 months] and 2.6 months [95% CI, 1.4 to 5.4 months], respectively). At 6 months, 55% of the high-TMB subgroup remained progression-free vs 31% in the low-TMB subgroup.  The cut-off of 10 mut/Mb was selected for this retrospective analysis as the ORR exceeded 40% which was higher than historical chemotherapy responses, and a higher TMB cutoff did not result in additional improvement. Further prospective validation in a larger randomized study is required to validate this selected cut-off and its predicative effect for nivolumab plus low-dose ipilimumab in NSCLC.
name: EID12588

source.title: First-Line Nivolumab Plus Ipilimumab in Advanced Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer (CheckMate 568): Outcomes by Programmed Death Ligand 1 and Tumor Mutational Burden as Biomarkers.

description:
In this 2009 study, the authors included 336 chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) patients at diagnosis, of which 25 patients (7.44%) exhibited variant Philadelphia (Ph) chromosome translocations. A control group of patients with the standard t(9;22) translocation was used for comparison. Conventional cytogenetics and fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) were utilized to characterize the variant translocations and investigate deletions on the derivative chromosome 9 [der(9)].
Variant Ph translocations, involving chromosomes 9, 22, and one or more additional chromosomes, were identified in all 25 cases. The BCR::ABL1 fusion gene was detected in all patients, confirming the diagnosis of CML despite the complex karyotypes. Deletions adjacent to the ABL1 gene on der(9) were observed in 15 of the 25 cases (60%), a significantly greater proportion than that found in typical Ph translocations (12–15%). The genesis of these variants was attributed to both one-step (36%) and two-step (56%) mechanisms, with the latter being more prevalent. The cohort was composed of patients where any chromosome could be involved, with breakpoints preferentially located in the CG-richest regions of the genome.
The authors concluded that the BCR::ABL1 fusion is the fundamental diagnostic event in CML, even in cases with complex variant translocations. They identified that these variant translocations are associated with a markedly higher incidence of deletions on der(9). Proper assessment of the prognostic significance of these variants requires categorization based on their mechanism of genesis and 9q34 deletion status.
name: EID12589

source.title: Molecular cytogenetic characterization of variant Philadelphia translocations in chronic myeloid leukemia: genesis and deletion of derivative chromosome 9.

description: A small case series examined molecular features along with clinicopathologic and immunohistochemical characteristics of sarcomas with EWSR1::NFATC2 gene fusions. The study included 6 cases (5 males and 1 female; age range 24-67 years), comprising 3 male cases of primary bone tumors of the radius and the remaining 3 cases involving primary soft tissue tumors. A dual-color, EWSR1 break-apart probe set (chr22q12 proximal and distal probes) detected EWSR1 rearrangement and concurrent amplification of its 5'-region in all cases. The EWSR1::NFATC2 gene fusion was confirmed using the corresponding FISH probes. RT-PCR followed by Sanger sequencing identified the fusion joining the 5'-end of EWSR1 (exon 7) and 3'-end of NFATC2 (exon 3). Together, the recurrent EWSR1::NFATC2 fusion identified a novel entity of small round cell sarcoma.

disease.name: Round Cell Sarcoma With EWSR1-non-ETS Fusion

name: EID12590

source.title: EWSR1-NFATC2 Translocation-associated Sarcoma Clinicopathologic Findings in a Rare Aggressive Primary Bone or Soft Tissue Tumor.

description: This landmark study represents the first description of the EWSR1::NFATC2 fusion in Ewing-like sarcomas, leading to the establishment of 'round cell sarcoma with EWSR1-non-ETS fusions' as a new disease entity in the 2020 WHO Classification of Soft Tissue and Bone Tumors. Four male cases (aged 16-39 years) of primary bone tumors were included; all expressed an in-frame EWSR1::NFATC2 fusion transcript. Array-CGH (n=3 cases) and interphase FISH (n=1 case) revealed amplification of chromosomes 22q12 and 20q13. RT-PCR followed by Sanger sequencing revealed fusion between exon 8 of EWSR1 and exon 3 of NFATC2. Using the fiber-FISH technique, the genomic breakpoints were mapped to intron 8 of EWSR1 (22q12) and intron 2 of NFATC2 (20q13). Mechanistically, this fusion results in loss of the N-terminal regulatory region and replacement of a weak nuclear localization signal (NLS) of NFATC2 with a strong NLS of EWSR1, leading to an uncontrolled nuclear localization and activation of the chimera protein.

disease.name: Round Cell Sarcoma With EWSR1-non-ETS Fusion
