source.title: The NFATc2 gene is involved in a novel cloned translocation in a Ewing sarcoma variant that couples its function in immunology to oncology.

description: This study analyzed over 300 patient with advanced solid tumors and melanoma across 22 tumor types from four KEYNOTE clinical trials to define genomic and immune predictors of response to pembrolizumab (anti–PD-1 immunotherapy). Using whole-exome sequencing and NanoString gene profiling, they evaluated tumor mutational burden (TMB) and the T cell–inflamed gene expression profile (GEP) in formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded pretreatment samples. TMB cut-off values for the pan-tumor and single-indication clinical cohorts were the Youden Index values derived in AUROC analysis (102.5 for pan-cancer, 86 for HNSCC, and 191.5 for melanoma group). TMB and GEP profiles were also analyzed within The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) database of 6384 tumors and the WES cut-off >100 mutations per exome was chosen for high TMB to match the Youden TBM pan-cancer cut-offs. TMB and GEP were independently predictive of clinical response and progression-free survival in KEYNOTE cohorts, and together they stratified patients into four biologically distinct subgroups: those with high TMB/high GEP had the highest objective response rates (37–57%), and the longest progression-free survival, whereas those with low TMB/high GEP or high TMB/low GEP showed moderate response rate (12-35% and 11-42%, respectively), and patients with low TMB/low GEP tumors rarely responded (0–9%). The two markers were only weakly correlated (Spearman correlation coefficient at r ~ 0.2), indicating that TMB and GEP are independent predictive markers, with TMB capturing neoantigen load, while GEP reflecting T-cell activation within the tumor microenvironment. Integrative analyses of TCGA data confirmed these findings and revealed resistance-associated alterations such as mutation in STK11, KEAP1, and APC in high TMB and low GEP lung and colorectal cancers, but not in the pan-cancer analysis. In addition, TMB highly correlated with neoantigen load in pan-cancer cohort (r=0.87), HNSCC (r=0.83), and melanoma cohort (r=0.9). Overall, the study established TMB and GEP as complementary, tumor-agnostic predictors of benefit from PD-1 blockade and provided a framework for precision immunotherapy and biomarker-guided combination strategies.
name: EID12594

source.title: Pan-tumor genomic biomarkers for PD-1 checkpoint blockade-based immunotherapy.

description: In the TIMER dataset, levels of MMP1 is increased in cancers compared with normal tissue, where its levels in sacituzumab govitecan (SG)-resistant tumours are higher than SG-sensitive tumours by IHC. In the TCGA database, high levels of MMP1 is associated with poor prognosis in patients with hormone-positive breast cancer.  Breast cancer cell lines (MCF-7 and T47D) slowly exposed to, and eventually becoming resistant to sacituzumab govitecan exhibit mesenchymal-like morphology and increased mRNA expression of MMP1.  MMP1 overexpression in SG-resistant breast cancer cell lines is associated with increased colony formation and migration. Mechanistically, MMP1 induces EMT rhough NF-kB pathway activation, while inhibition of MMP1 overcomes SG resistance in pre-clinical models. Together, these evidence shows that MMP1 overexpression is associated with SG resistance.
name: EID12597

source.title: MMP1-induced NF-κB activation promotes epithelial-mesenchymal transition and sacituzumab govitecan resistance in hormone receptor-positive breast cancer.

description:
The Phase 3 trial for the selective and brain-penetrant RET kinase inhibitor selpercatinib in Medullary Thyroid Cancer (MTC) LIBRETTO-531 (NCT04211337) consisted of 291 total patients. 

The patients had pathologically confirmed unresectable locally advanced or metastatic MTC, and had no history of treatment with kinase inhibitors. 

Patients had a prospectively identified pathogenic RET alteration, either somatic or germline, and 182 patients had RET M918T (~63%). 

From the patients with M918T, 121 were treated with selpercatinib, and 61 were treated with control (physician’s choice of vandetanib or cabozantinib).  

In the M918T subgroup analysis, control patients had median progression-free survival (PFS) of 17.5 months, while in the selpercatinib-treated patients the median PFS was not met.  Hazard Ratio (95% CI) was 0.40 (0.21–0.77) between M918T control and selpercatinib treated patients.
name: EID12598

source.title: Phase 3 Trial of Selpercatinib in Advanced RET-Mutant Medullary Thyroid Cancer.

description: In a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled biomarker-selected adjuvant study (ALASCCA, NCT02647099; colorectal carcinoma; n = 626; group A: PIK3CA exon 9/20, n = 314), aspirin 160 mg daily (group A n = 157) for 3 years reduced colorectal cancer recurrence vs placebo (group A n = 157) in the PIK3CA hotspot subgroup (3-yr cumulative incidence 7.7% vs 14.1%; HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.24 - 0.98; P = 0.04) with 3-yr DFS 88.5% vs 81.4% (HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.34 - 1.08). Severe AEs occurred in 16.8% vs 11.6% with events including GI bleeding and subarachnoid hemorrhage, and one out of the 4 observed deaths was deemed possibly related to aspirin; OS at 5 yr was not significantly different (91.6% vs 90.1%; HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.37 - 1.68).

description: This part of the open-label multipart phase 3 trial, CheckMate 277 (Trial ID: 29658845), examined the performance of nivolumab plus ipilimumab compared to chemotherapy among non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients with a high tumour mutational burden (TMB) (>= 10 mutations/ megabase). Stage IV/ recurrent NSCLC patients that were chemotherapy treatment naïve were recruited. Patients with tumour programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression of at least 1% were randomly assigned to receive nivolumab plus ipilimumab, nivolumab monotherapy, or chemotherapy; while those with tumour PD-L1 expression of < 1% were randomly assigned to be treated with nivolumab plus ipilimumab, nivolumab plus chemotherapy, or chemotherapy. Tissue TMB was determined by the FoundationOne CDx assay. Patients with high TMB achieved significantly longer progression-free survival (PFS) with nivolumab plus ipilimumab (n = 139) (1-year PFS of 42%, median PFS of 7.2 months with 95% confidence interval [CI], 5.5 to 13.2), compared to chemotherapy alone (n = 160) (1-year PFS of 13.2%, median PFS of 5.5 months with 95% CI, 4.4 to 5.8) (hazard ratio [HR] 0.58; 97.5% CI, 0.41 to 0.81; P<0.001). 45.3% of patients achieved objective response with nivolumab plus ipilimumab, compared to 26.9% with chemotherapy. The benefit of nivolumab plus ipilimumab over chemotherapy was consistent across histologic subtypes and despite whether the tumour PD-L1 expression was at least 1% or lower than 1%. On the contrary, among the patients with low TMB, the clinical benefit was not significantly different between patients treated with nivolumab plus ipilimumab (n= 191) (median PFS of 3.2 months with 95% CI, 2.7 to 4.3) and those treated with chemotherapy (n=189) (median PFS of 5.5 months with 95% CI, 4.3 to 5.6) (HR 1.07; 95% CI, 0.84 to 1.35). In conclusion, this study demonstrated significant clinical benefit of first-line nivolumab plus ipilimumab over chemotherapy among NSCLC patients with a high TMB, irrespective of the expression level of tumour PD-L1.
name: EID12614

source.title: Nivolumab plus Ipilimumab in Lung Cancer with a High Tumor Mutational Burden.

description:
In a multinational open label phase II dose randomized study of sunvozertinib in platinum pretreated advanced NSCLC with EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations (WU-KONG1B, NCT03974022; efficacy n = 85 for 200 mg-random, n = 89 for 300 mg-random, and n = 107 for 300 mg-all), sunvozertinib produced IRC confirmed ORRs of 45.9% (97.5% CI, 33.6 - 58.5), 47.2% (97.5% CI, 35.1 - 59.5), and 45.8% (97.5% CI, 34.8 - 57.0) at 200 mg-random, 300 mg-random, and 300 mg-all, respectively (P < 0.0001 vs null ORR 17%), with median PFS 8.4, 7.7, and 6.9 months and 12-month OS rates 62.1, 73.7, and 69.4%. Across the 200 mg-random and 300 mg-random cohorts, the 770_SVD subtype represented 24.7% and 18.0% of patients, with cORRs of 47.6% and 56.3%, respectively. Meanwhile, the 769_ASV subtype accounted for 21.2% and 23.6%, with cORRs of 33.3% and 57.1%, respectively. 
Across treated patients (200 mg-random n = 91; 300 mg-all n = 111), grade ≥3 treatment related AEs occurred in 40.7% and 58.6%, most commonly diarrhea (2.2% vs 18.0%), blood CPK increase (6.6% vs 12.6%), and anemia (4.4% vs 6.3%), with no treatment related deaths; both dose levels met the prespecified primary endpoint of IRC confirmed ORR.
name: EID12623

source.title: Phase II Dose-Randomized Study of Sunvozertinib in Platinum-Pretreated Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer With Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor Exon 20 Insertion Mutations (WU-KONG1B).

description:
In a multinational open label phase II dose randomized study of sunvozertinib in platinum pretreated advanced NSCLC with EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations (WU-KONG1B, NCT03974022; efficacy n = 85 for 200 mg-random, n = 89 for 300 mg-random, and n = 107 for 300 mg-all), sunvozertinib produced IRC confirmed ORRs of 45.9% (97.5% CI, 33.6 - 58.5), 47.2% (97.5% CI, 35.1 - 59.5), and 45.8% (97.5% CI, 34.8 - 57.0) at 200 mg-random, 300 mg-random, and 300 mg-all, respectively (P < 0.0001 vs null ORR 17%), with median PFS 8.4, 7.7, and 6.9 months and 12-month OS rates 62.1, 73.7, and 69.4%.  Exon20ins variants grouped as “Others” comprised 48.2% and 53.9% of patients in the 200 mg‐random and 300 mg‐random cohorts with cORRs of 46.3% and 39.6%, respectively.
Across treated patients (200 mg-random n = 91; 300 mg-all n = 111), grade ≥3 treatment related AEs occurred in 40.7% and 58.6%, most commonly diarrhea (2.2% vs 18.0%), blood CPK increase (6.6% vs 12.6%), and anemia (4.4% vs 6.3%), with no treatment related deaths; both dose levels met the prespecified primary endpoint of IRC confirmed ORR.

In the TCGA-LUAD cohort without immunotherapy (n = 507), PFS (p = 0.43) and OS (p = 0.16) did not differ by LRP1B status, indicating the survival advantage was specific to ICI treatment.

description: In this study the authors examined six gynecologic tract perivascular epithelioid cell tumors (PEComas) that were previously diagnosed as PEComa but demonstrated unusual morphology suggestive of TFE3 involvement. A comparison group of eleven conventional PEComas was also included. TFE3 break-apart FISH and immunohistochemistry were utilized to evaluate for TFE3 gene abnormalities. TFE3 rearrangements were identified in all six test cases, whereas none of the conventional PEComas showed TFE3 rearrangement. The TFE3-rearranged tumors showed a distinctive immunophenotype characterized by strong nuclear TFE3 expression, absent or minimal melanocytic marker expression, and lack of smooth muscle marker positivity, in contrast to the conventional PEComa profile. Morphologically, TFE3-rearranged PEComas demonstrated predominantly pure epithelioid clear-cell morphology with an alveolar or nested growth pattern, differing from the mixed epithelioid–spindled architecture typical of conventional lesions. The cohort included five females and one male, aged 17–52 years. The authors concluded that they have identified a distinct subset of PEComas with characteristic morphology and immunophenotype, defined by v::TFE3 gene fusions, which separate them diagnostically from conventional PEComa and support their classification within the family of TFE3-associated neoplasms.
name: EID12690

source.title: TFE3 translocation-associated perivascular epithelioid cell neoplasm (PEComa) of the gynecologic tract: morphology, immunophenotype, differential diagnosis.

description: In this 2025 study, the authors included 14 confirmed TFE3-rearranged perivascular epithelioid cell tumors (PEComas), previously classified as benign (9 tumors) or malignant (5 tumors), and compared them to the molecular features of TSC2/1-inactivated PEComas. DNA sequencing and FISH were utilized to investigate genetic correlates of malignancy. Complex chromosomal copy number alterations (CNAs) were detected in three of four (75%) assessable malignant tumors and were absent in all benign tumors. Inactivating alterations in TP53, RB1, or ATRX were rare among the malignant tumors, observed in only 1 of 5 cases, contrasting with patterns seen in malignant TSC2/1-inactivated PEComas. The cohort comprised 11 females and 3 males, with a wide age range at diagnosis, from 9 to 64 years (median 31.5 years). Tumors occurred in diverse anatomical sites, including the uterus, extremities, colon, nasal cavity, neck, retroperitoneum, bladder, and ovary. The authors concluded that complex CNAs are a frequent genetic correlate of malignancy in TFE3-rearranged PEComas and may serve as a diagnostic marker, and that these tumors lack the highly recurrent TP53, RB1, or ATRX alterations characteristic of TSC2/1-inactivated PEComas.
name: EID12691

source.title: Genetic correlates of malignancy in TFE3-rearranged PEComa: a series of 14 cases.

description: This case series presented 7 NFATC2-rearranged sarcomas, including 4 EWSR1::NFATC2 and 3 FUS::NFATC2 cases, and developed an ACAN-encoding aggrecan immunohistochemistry as a diagnostic tool for these tumors. All cases were primary bone tumors with 6 located in the long bones (4 femur, 2 tibia) and 1 in the ilium. Using RNA-seq, the FUS::NFATC2 fusion was found to join exon 6 of FUS with exon 3 of NFATC2 in all three cases. FISH analysis using the FUS break-apart probe (BAP) was applied to one case and identified an unbalanced pattern with gains of the 5’ FISH probe (data not shown). Array-CGH further showed more complex genomic profiles in all FUS::NFATC2 cases compared with one tested EWSR1::NFATC2 sample. This study expanded the evidence for the recurrent FUS::NFATC2 fusion in the rare round cell sarcoma.

description: This is the first study to identify the FUS::NFATC2 gene fusion. Using multi-omics approach and targeted sequencing, the authors comprehensively characterized the molecular landscape of a large cohort of Ewing sarcoma (-like) tumors (101 samples, including 65 tumors and 36 cell lines). Seven of 62 (11.3%) tumors analyzed by RNA-seq were found to lack a typical Ewing sarcoma EWSR1 gene fusion. One case was found to harbor a novel, in-frame FUS::NFATC2 fusion joining the TET family member FUS (exon 6) and the non-ETS family transcription factor NFATC2 (exon 9). This observation was further verified by RT-PCR followed by Sanger sequencing. This work provided the first evidence of FUS::NFATC2 gene fusion, which leads to the establishment of the new disease entity “round cell sarcoma with EWSR1-non-ETS fusions”.

description:
In a pooled analysis of five phase I–II trials and an expanded access program of ONC201 (dordaviprone) for recurrent H3 K27M–mutant diffuse midline glioma (NCT02525692, NCT03295396, NCT03416530, NCT03134131, NCT05392374; n = 50), the RANO-HGG ORR was 20.0% (1 CR, 9 PR; 95% CI 10.0–33.7) with DCR 40.0% (95% CI 26.4–54.8; SD n = 10), median DOR 11.2 months (95% CI 3.8–NR), TTR 8.3 months (range 1.9–15.9), 6-month PFS 35.1% (95% CI 21.2–49.3), and median OS 13.7 months (95% CI 8.0–20.3), with 12- and 24-month OS of 57.3% (95% CI 41.4–70.3) and 34.7% (95% CI 20.7–49.2). 
Using RANO-LGG criteria, the ORR was 26.0% (95% CI 14.6–40.3; 6 PR, 7 MR) and DCR 42.0% (95% CI, 28.2 to 56.8; SD, n = 8), and when combining the best responses across either RANO system, the ORR was 30.0% (95% CI 17.9–44.6) and DCR 44.0% (95% CI, 30.0–58.7; SD, n = 7); corticosteroid reduction ≥50% occurred in 46.7% of evaluable patients (7/15; 95% CI, 21.3–73.4), median TTR 3.7 months (range 1.9–5.6) and KPS/LPS improvement in 20.6% (7/34, 95% CI, 8.7 to 37.9) median TTR 3.5 months (range 1.9–22.4).

description:
In this 2025 retrospective study, 14 spindle cell rhabdomyosarcoma (SCRMS) cases previously identified as possessing ZFP64::NCOA2 or ZFP64::NCOA3 fusions were pulled from clinical archives to assess clinicopathologic, immunohistochemical, and molecular genetic features. Key observations include a strong male prevalence, middle-age occurrence (median 41 years; range 22-81 years), wide anatomic distribution, and NCOA3 fusions are more common than NCOA2 fusions. Arising primarily from soft tissue, these tumors displayed both fascicular and spindle cell morphologies within a hyalinized collagenous background and various degrees of skeletal muscle marker expression, although occasional focal or diffuse round cell morphologies were also observed. 

All cases were analyzed by targeted RNA sequencing platforms from various laboratories, with specific fusions noted between ZFP64 exon 5::NCOA2 exon 14 fusion in 6 cases (43%) and ZFP64 exon 5::NCOA3 exon 14/15 fusion in 8 cases (57%). Ten of these cases were also characterized by DNA methylation profiling, revealing ZFP64 SCRMS as an epigenetic sarcoma subtype distinct from other RMS. SCRMS with ZFP64::NCOA2/3 fusions are associated with frequent distant metastases, local recurrences, and death, and therefore these fusions may provide benefit as prognostic markers.
name: EID12699

source.title: Clinicopathologic and Molecular Genetic Features of Spindle Cell Rhabdomyosarcoma Harboring ZFP64::NCOA2/3 Fusions: A Series of 14 Cases.

description: In this study of 21 patients with FGFR-driven urothelial carcinoma treated with selective FGFR inhibitors (including erdafitinib), post-progression molecular analyses (tissue and/or ctDNA sequencing) identified secondary FGFR3 kinase domain mutations as a mechanism of acquired resistance. In one patient (MR86) who initially harbored FGFR3 S249C and PIK3CA E545K and was treated with erdafitinib (best response −25%; progression-free survival 2.7 months), an FGFR3 N540K mutation was detected in post-progression tumor tissue but was absent at baseline, indicating emergence during therapy. Functional studies using Ba/F3 models demonstrated that the FGFR3 N540K mutation reduces sensitivity to FGFR inhibitors, including erdafitinib, supporting its role as a resistance-associated alteration.

description: In this study of patients with FGFR-driven urothelial carcinoma treated with selective FGFR inhibitors, longitudinal ctDNA analysis identified emergent FGFR3 kinase domain mutations at disease progression. In one patient (CTC1845) with an activating FGFR3 Y373C mutation who received sequential treatment with erdafitinib followed by futibatinib (with intervening immunotherapy), post-progression ctDNA profiling detected the FGFR3 N540K mutation (VAF 4%) alongside additional kinase domain mutations (V555L, L608V). Functional analyses in Ba/F3 models demonstrated that FGFR3 N540K reduces sensitivity to multiple FGFR inhibitors, including erdafitinib and futibatinib, supporting its role in acquired resistance under sequential FGFR-targeted therapy.

description: Ba/F3 cells expressing the FGFR3::TACC3 fusion with or without the N540K mutation were treated with multiple FGFR inhibitors, including erdafitinib and futibatinib. In parental Ba/F3 cells, the IC50 values were 1352.2 nM for erdafitinib and 8588.7 nM for futibatinib, whereas in cells expressing FGFR3::TACC3 alone, IC50 values were 0.02 nM and 0.03 nM, respectively. In Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR3::TACC3 with the N540K mutation, IC50 values increased to 25.9 nM for erdafitinib and 19.5 nM for futibatinib. Across the inhibitor panel, IC50 values exceeded 100 nmol/L for all agents except erdafitinib and futibatinib.

description:
In the phase 1/2 trial LIBRETTO-121 (NCT03899792), for patients 0.5-21 yrs old with advanced RET-altered solid tumors, dosing started at 92 mg/m2 twice a day of Selpercatinib.

Patients had RET-mutant medullary thyroid cancer (MTC, n = 14), RET fusion-positive papillary thyroid cancer (PTC, n = 10), or other tumors (n = 3).

M918T was the most common mutation in MTC (10/14) and NCOA4-RET fusion most common in PTC (5/10).


Treatment ranged from 0.4 to 40.8 months, and 22 pts remained on treatment at time of this report. 

Overall response rate was 10/12 in patients with measurable disease at baseline, with 1 having stable disease and 1 with progressive disease. No PTC or MTC patients had progressive disease. At median follow up of 18 months, the median progression free survival had not yet been reached.
name: EID12708

description: Two novel somatic interstitial in-frame deletions in RET, with unknown transformation potential, were identified in medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) tumor samples. One of these (RET E632_L633del) was compared to already established variants (as positive controls) including RET M918T, which authors describe as typical of MEN2B phenotype familial MTC and as a frequent somatic mutation in sporadic MTC. In-vitro transforming activity was tested using focus formation assays on NIH3T3 cells. Vectors for control, M918T, and E632_L633del with neomycin resistance were made and expressed in NIH3T3, and selection with G418 performed. 1.4 x 10^4 M918T and 9.6 x 10^3 control colonies (colonies/ug DNA used in transfection) survived G418 selection. 1.8 x 10^2 transformed loci formed for M918T cells, but <1 x 10^–2 formed for wildtype control. This ratio was 0.013 transformed loci per M918T colony.
name: EID12709

source.title: Somatic in frame deletions not involving juxtamembranous cysteine residues strongly activate the RET proto-oncogene.

description: A total of 56 metastatic medullary thyroid cancer cases (50 sporadic, 6 familial) were analyzed for RET mutations. A total of 7 cases were found to have a RET germline mutations however one case had a mutation previously shown to have low transforming potential and was considered sporadic. 34/50 sporadic cases had M918T mutations and 3/6 familial cases carried a RET M918T germline mutation. All three showed local recurrences/metastases, and one had instances of pheochromocytoma.

description: The use of circulating tumor DNA in blood for TMB assessment was tested. The cancer gene panel NCC-GP150, which covers the whole exon regions of 150 genes, was created and tested for correlation against established methods for TMB assessment. Testing compared whole exome sequencing (WES) results from tissue samples of 48 Chinese advanced NSCLC patients with NCC-GP150 from matched blood samples from those patients. A Spearman correlation of 0.62 (P<0.001) was reported between these results, when the cutoff between high and low blood TMB (H-bTMB) was greater or equal to 6. In a test with 33 different cancer types, NCC-GP150 correlated strongly with established WES results in 25/33 of the tumor types. 50 advanced NSCLC patients were treated with PD-1 or PDL-1 inhibition. When the H-bTMB cutoff was set to 6, then a minimum hazard ratio favoring H-bTMB patients was seen of HR=0.39 (0.18-0.84) P=.02. For the subset of patients with anti-PD1/PD-L1 therapy as first- or second-Line treatment, results were stronger with HR=0.08 (0.02-0.36) P=.001 at a cutoff of H-bTMB of 6. In this subgroup overall response rate was significantly different (P=0.003), 61.1% in H-b-TMB and 6.7% in L-bTMB. Additionally, in responders bTMB was significantly higher (median 10) than in non responders (median 5, P=0.008). The authors conclude that  ctDNA-based bTMB measured using the NCC-GP150 panel is a potential biomarker for anti–PD-1 and anti–PD-L1 treatment in NSCLC.
name: EID12724

source.title: Assessment of Blood Tumor Mutational Burden as a Potential Biomarker for Immunotherapy in Patients With Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer With Use of a Next-Generation Sequencing Cancer Gene Panel.

description: In this 2022 study, the authors included 40 patients aged ≤12 months diagnosed with spindle cell rhabdomyosarcoma (SCRMS) enrolled in international trials and registries, of whom 39 presented with localized disease. FISH or RT-PCR was utilized to investigate VGLL2 and NCOA2 gene fusions. Among 26 tumors with available molecular evaluation, VGLL2 and/or NCOA2 gene rearrangements were detected in 13 (50%) cases. These included NCOA2-VGLL2 fusions in 2 tumours, NCOA2-related fusions (TEAD1-NCOA2) in 5, and VGLL2-related fusions (VGLL2-CITED2) in 6. No gene fusion was identified in 12 cases, and the remaining 14 cases were not tested or had insufficient tissue. The cohort was composed of 18 females and 21 males, with a median age at diagnosis of 2.5 months. The authors concluded that they have identified a subset of spindle cell rhabdomyosarcoma occurring in infants, in which recurrent VGLL2 and NCOA2 gene fusions are present in half of the cases with available molecular data, supporting their role in the biology of infantile SCRMS.
name: EID12727

source.title: Congenital spindle cell rhabdomyosarcoma: An international cooperative analysis.

description: In this 2013 study, the authors included 21 spindle cell and sclerosing rhabdomyosarcomas (RMS), and a control group of 4 embryonal RMS and 3 ectomesenchymomas. RNA sequencing and FISH were utilized to investigate NCOA2 gene abnormalities. NCOA2 gene rearrangements were detected in 3 of the 10 pediatric spindle cell RMS (in a 4-week-old, 3-month-old, and 7-month-old) and not detected in any of the tumors from older children, adults, sclerosing RMS, or the control group. SRF::NCOA2 fusions were present in one tumor, and TEAD1::NCOA2 fusions were identified in another, with RT-PCR confirming fusion of SRF exon 6 with NCOA2 exon 12 in the first case. The cohort was composed of 2 females and 1 male, all under one year of age, with tumors arising in the chest wall or posterior neck. The authors concluded that they have identified a subset of spindle cell rhabdomyosarcoma occurring almost exclusively in infants, characterized by recurrent NCOA2 gene rearrangements, which distinguishes it from morphologically similar tumors in older patients.
name: EID12731

source.title: Recurrent NCOA2 gene rearrangements in congenital/infantile spindle cell rhabdomyosarcoma.

description:
In the phase I study of pazopanib and vorinostat in 36 patients with advanced solid tumors, detection of hotspot TP53 mutation was associated with a higher rate of SD ≥6 months/PR, longer median PFS (months), and longer median OS (months) compared to patients without a hotspot TP53 mutation. 
In colorectal cancer cases, detected TP53 hotspot mutations included TP53 R213*, TP53 G245S, and TP53 R273C.

In the subgroup of patients with metastatic colorectal cancer and sarcoma treated with pazopanib and vorinostat, those with detected hotspot TP53 mutations (n = 6) had a significantly longer median PFS of 6.5 months (95% CI 3.0–9.0; p = 0.023) compared to 2.0 months (95% CI 1.8–2.2; p = 0.023) in TP53-undetected cases (n = 10), and a significantly longer median OS of 19.8 months (95% CI 8.2–31.4; p = 0.021) versus 7.2 months (95% CI 0.6–13.8; p = 0.021), respectively.

description: This case series study reported 11 neoplasms harboring the EWSR1::PATZ1 gene fusion with 7 in the soft tissue and 4 in the brain. Paired-end sequencing identified a somatic intra-chromosomal paracentric inversion on chromosome 22 involving EWSR1 and PATZ1, located ~2 Mb apart, in all cases. This rearrangement permits transcription of both genes in the same orientation. Two soft tissue cases,1 myoepithelial carcinoma and 1 undifferentiated low-grade sarcoma, were further characterized by RT-PCR with Sanger sequencing. In the former case, EWSR1 exon 8 was fused to PATZ1 exon 1 with a 28-nucleotide insertion derived from EWSR1 intron 8 encoding 10 amino acids. In the latter case, EWSR1 exon 8 was also fused to PATZ1 exon 1, with concurrent presence of an in-frame deletion within exon 1 sequence. Further comprehensive molecular profiling revealed loss/deletion of CDKN2A/CDKN2B in 5 of 7 soft tissue cases (71.4%), with 1 showing concurrent MDM2 amplification. This study expanded the evidence for the recurrent EWSR1::PATZ1 fusion in small round cell sarcoma.

disease.name: Round Cell Sarcoma With EWSR1-non-ETS Fusion

source.title: Clinical, pathological, and genomic features of EWSR1-PATZ1 fusion sarcoma.

description: This case series study presented clinical, histopathological, and molecular findings of 9 EWSR1::PATZ1-rearranged sarcomas, including one previously reported case. The cohort included 4 males and 5 females ranging in age from 10 to 81 years. These tumors most occurred in the thoracoabdominal soft tissues (5 in abdominal wall soft tissues, 3 in the thorax, 1 in the posterior neck). Molecularly, the EWSR1 (exon8)::PATZ1(exon 1) gene fusion, with or without the inclusion of part of EWSR1 intron 8, was identified in all cases by NGS. Select cases were subjected to FISH analyses. All 4 tested cases (8/100 nuclei in 3 cases; 9/100 nuclei in 1 case) showed EWSR1 break-apart signals, yet none reached the diagnostic cutoff (10% positive nuclei). Combined FISH and NGS analyses further revealed CDKN2A homozygous or heterozygous deletion in 3 of 6 cases. Chart review and pathological examination showed diverse clinical courses and a broad morphologic spectrum. Collectively, EWSR1::PATZ1 sarcomas are clinically and morphologically heterogeneous diseases, and FISH is an suboptimal for the detection of the EWSR1 rearrangement in this disease.

description: This study presented molecular and clinicopathologic findings of a cohort of 17 EWSR1::PATZ1 soft tissue sarcomas. These tumors occurred in 12 males and 5 females with 15-71 years of age (median age, 50 years) and involved the thoracoabdominal soft tissues (14 cases; 82%), lower extremities (2 cases; 12%), and tongue (1 case; 6%). Targeted RNA sequencing identified EWSR1::PATZ1 gene fusions in all cases, with variable breakpoints located within exon 7-9 of EWSR1, with exon 8 being the predominant breakpoint (14/17, 82%), fused to exon 1 of PATZ1. Genomic breakpoints were obtained from 12 cases showing multiple junction configurations of the EWSR1::PATZ1 gene fusion at the genomic level. The study also showed broad morphological features with more favorable outcome than previously described for EWSR1::PATZ1 positive sarcomas. Notably, this study had two times more male than female patients, although no male predominance had been described previously for the EWSR1::PATZ1 fusion sarcomas.

description:
In this 2015 study, formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue samples were retrieved from the diagnostic pathology archives of the Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital (RNOH) and the Basel Bone Tumour Reference Centre (BBTRC). All cases were reviewed by specialist bone tumour pathologists and classified according to World Health Organization (WHO) criteria. To investigate the oncogenic driver of Giant Cell Tumour of Bone (GCT), whole-genome sequencing was performed on five cases and whole-exome sequencing on one case. In addition, targeted hotspot sequencing using a 14-gene panel, including H3F3A and H3F3B, was conducted to assess the specificity of the p.G34W alteration. This analysis included 91 GCTs and 321 other osteoclast-rich bone lesions.
No driver mutations other than the H3F3A p.G34W mutation were identified in the sequenced genomes and exome. Targeted sequencing detected this mutation in 83 GCT cases, with single cases of H3F3A p.G34R and p.G34M; no mutations were found in H3F3B. Both GCTs that metastasized to the lung harbored the H3F3A p.G34W mutation. Overall, H3F3A p.G34 alterations were present in 96% (85/89) of GCTs and absent in other bone tumours in this cohort, supporting their role as highly sensitive and specific molecular markers for GCT.
name: EID12749

source.title: Diagnostic value of H3F3A mutations in giant cell tumour of bone compared to osteoclast-rich mimics.

description:
In this 2015 study, formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tumor samples diagnosed between 1996 and 2014 as giant cell tumor of bone (GCTB), chondroblastoma, chondromyxoid fibroma, aneurysmal bone cyst, or telangiectatic osteosarcoma were retrieved from the Leiden University Medical Centre. A total of 75 GCTB samples were analyzed, including 15 recurrences from 12 patients. H3F3A hotspot mutations were assessed using Sanger sequencing, and immunohistochemistry for H3K36 trimethylation and ATRX expression was performed to evaluate correlation with mutation status.
H3F3A G34W/V mutations were identified in 41 of 59 GCTBs (69%) (39 G34W, 2 G34V). Rare variants included a G34 stop codon and a TCT insertion at position 35. H3K36 trimethylation was present in 59 of 60 cases and was more frequent in mutated tumors, whereas ATRX loss showed no correlation with mutation status. Only G34W/V variants were considered mutation-positive for correlation analysis due to the uncertain significance of other variants. In conclusion, H3F3A mutation analysis (particularly G34W/V) by Sanger sequencing represents a highly specific, though less sensitive, diagnostic tool for distinguishing GCTB from other giant cell–containing bone tumors.
name: EID12750

source.title: Mutation Analysis of H3F3A and H3F3B as a Diagnostic Tool for Giant Cell Tumor of Bone and Chondroblastoma.

description: In this study, the authors investigated a case of pseudomyogenic hemangioendothelioma in a 33-year-old woman presenting with multifocal lytic bone lesions. Previous studies had demonstrated recurrent SERPINE1::FOSB and ACTB::FOSB fusions in pseudomyogenic hemangioendothelioma; however, this tumor lacked those known rearrangements. Using RNA sequencing, RT-PCR, and Sanger sequencing, the authors identified a novel in-frame WWTR1::FOSB fusion, joining exon 4 of WWTR1 (3q25) to exon 2 of FOSB (19q13). The fusion transcript places FOSB under the control of the WWTR1 promoter and is predicted to encode a 553-amino-acid chimeric WWTR1::FOSB transcription factor. Immunohistochemistry demonstrated strong nuclear FOSB expression in the tumor cells, supporting fusion-driven overexpression. Cytogenetic analysis showed a normal karyotype, highlighting the utility of RNA-based methods in detecting cryptic rearrangements. The authors conclude that, in addition to SERPINE1::FOSB and ACTB::FOSB, WWTR1::FOSB represents another recurrent FOSB-related fusion in pseudomyogenic hemangioendothelioma. Detection of FOSB rearrangements and associated nuclear FOSB overexpression may serve as a valuable diagnostic marker to distinguish pseudomyogenic hemangioendothelioma from its histologic mimics.
name: EID12752

source.title: Fusion of the Genes WWTR1 and FOSB in Pseudomyogenic Hemangioendothelioma.

description: In this 2017 study the authors included four cases of gastroblastoma with control cases of histologic mimics. Gastroblastoma patients were aged 9, 27, 28 and 56 years. RNASeq identified a MALAT1::GLI1 fusion in two gastroblastomas, with MALAT1 exon 1 fusing to GLI1 exons 5 or 6, and RT-PCR confirming the presence of the fusion. FISH was positive for rearrangement and fusion of the MALAT1 and GLI1 loci in all four cases. Of the contols, one plexiform fibromyxoma was positive for MALAT1 rearrangement but negative for GLI1 rearrangement, with all other controls negative for MALAT1::GLI1. Pathway analysis on differentially expressed genes identified upregulation of the Sonic hedgehog pathway. The authors conclude that gastroblastoma should exist as a distinct entity characterized by the presence of a somatic, recurrent, oncogenic MALAT1::GLI1 fusion gene.
name: EID12753

source.title: Gastroblastoma harbors a recurrent somatic MALAT1-GLI1 fusion gene.

description: In this 2023 case study the authors investigate a tumour with biphasic morphology composed of epithelial and spindle cell components, diagnosed in a 29-year-old woman. RT-PCR analysis revealed that the tumor harbored the MALAT1::GLI1 fusion gene. The authors also summarised the 16 cases of gastroblastoma that have been reported in the literature, with the MALAT::GLI1 fusion gene identified in 5 of these cases, with testing not performed in 9 cases and the 2 remaining cases showing EWSR1::CTBP1 and PTCH1::GLI2 fusions. They conclude that they have identified another case for this rare entity and postulate the potential role of targeted therapeutics, as nuclear expression of PD-L1 and HDAC2 was observed.
name: EID12754

source.title: Gastroblastoma mimics the embryonic mesenchyme of the foregut: a case report.

description: In this 2019 case study the authors investigate a gastric antral tumor with morphological, immunophenotypic and genotypic features consistent with gastroblastoma in a 79-year-old male. Molecular analysis identified a MALAT1::GLI1 fusion gene that retained exon 6 of GLI1. A previous "paraganglioma" detected in the patient was also found to harbor the MALAT1::GLI1 gene fusion, hence the present tumor was assumed to represent the relapse of a disease that ﬁrst presented at 74 years. The authors conclude that they have another example of a gastroblastoma, which is exceedingly rare, and have extended the known age range that this tumor can occur.
name: EID12755

source.title: Gastroblastoma in old age.

description: This exploratory analysis of the Phase 3 MYSTIC trial (NCT02453282) evaluated blood tumour mutational burden (bTMB) as a predictive biomarker for first-line durvalumab with or without tremelimumab vs chemotherapy in patients with advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The cfDNA assay used was GuardantOMNI (500 genes, 2.145 Mb) and the bTMB was calculated by identifying somatic synonymous and non-synonymous single nucleotide variants (SNVs) and short insertions/deletions (indels) at all variant allele frequencies. Pre-treatment plasma bTMB demonstrated a positive correlation with the patient-paired tissue TMB (tTMB) (Spearman rank correlation = 0.6, n=352). In the population evaluable for bTMB (n= 809), patients with bTMB ≥20 mut/Mb showed improved overall survival (OS) for durvalumab plus tremelimumab vs chemotherapy (median, 21.9 months vs 10.0 months; unadjusted HR, 0.49). The improved OS for durvalumab plus tremelimumab vs chemotherapy was not observed in patients with bTMB < 20 mut/Mb. Similarly, bTMB ≥20 mut/Mb, but not <20 mut/Mb, was also associated with improved PFS and ORR for durvalumab plus tremelimumab vs chemotherapy. These findings support a bTMB threshold of 20 mut/Mb as predictive of optimal clinical benefit in OS, PFS, and ORR for durvalumab with tremelimumab.
name: EID12760

source.title: Durvalumab With or Without Tremelimumab vs Standard Chemotherapy in First-line Treatment of Metastatic Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: The MYSTIC Phase 3 Randomized Clinical Trial.

description:
In ovarian carcinoma (OVCA) preclinical models, CCNE1 amplification predicted synergistic sensitivity to lunresertib (RP-6306) + camonsertib (RP-3500). CCNE1 copy number correlates with synergy by MTT assay (R² = 0.87, p = 0.0064) and ~80% growth inhibition at low-dose combination (RP-6306 31 nM + RP-3500 7.8 nM) in CCNE1-overexpressing cells.
The sensitive CCNE1-amplified OVCA cell lines were OVCAR3, FUOV1, COV318 (CN>5) and CCNE1 copy gain were OVCAR8, OVSAHO (CN 2-5).
In CCNE1-amplified OVCA PDX models (WO-19, WO-77), combination treatment (RP-6306 5–10 mg/kg + RP-3500 5 mg/kg) significantly increased tumor suppression and improved survival. This method of treatment also reduced metastases vs monotherapy (WO-19 metastases p = 0.0401 and p = 0.0122), with tumor progression (tumor volume > 1000 mm³) as the primary endpoint.

source.title: Targeting CCNE1 amplified ovarian and endometrial cancers by combined inhibition of PKMYT1 and ATR.

description:
In endometrial carcinoma (EMCA) preclinical models, CCNE1 amplification predicted synergistic sensitivity to lunresertib (RP-6306) + camonsertib (RP-3500), with ~80% growth inhibition at low-dose combination (RP-6306 31 nM + RP-3500 7.8 nM) in CCNE1-overexpressing cells and minimal effect in CCNE1-low parental models.
Sensitive CCNE1-amplified EMCA cell models included KLE, as well as CCNE1-induced WO-20 and SNU685 models.
In the CCNE1-amplified EMCA PDX model WU-115, RP-6306 (5–10 mg/kg) plus RP-3500 (5 mg/kg) induced tumor regressions and improved survival versus monotherapy (p = 0.0240–0.002 vs RP-6306; p = 0.0032–0.002 vs RP-3500), with tumor progression (tumor volume > 1000 mm³) as the primary endpoint.

In the breast carcinoma cohort of the phase II TAPUR trial (NCT02693535), patients with BRCA1/2 alterations treated with olaparib (26 evaluable) had 1 CR (BRCA2 loss), 11 PR (BRCA1 n=5, BRCA2 n=4, BRCA1/2 n=2), 6 SD16+ (BRCA1 n=1, BRCA2 n=4, BRCA1/2 n=1) yielding ORR 46% (95% CI, 27-67) and DCR 69% (90% CI 55-100; p < 0.001 vs null 15%). description: In this 2019 study, targeted RNA sequencing using the Archer FusionPlex technology was validated and implemented to detect oncogenic fusion transcripts in 62 genes recurrently rearranged in solid tumors, including sarcomas, without prior knowledge of fusion partners. A total of 192 formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) bone and soft tissue tumor samples from January 2016 to January 2018 were submitted to Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center for analysis. In-frame gene fusions were identified in 79 of 184 cases (43%), including 6 cases (3%) with novel fusion partners. In two cases of pseudomyogenic hemangioendothelioma present in this study cohort the testing revealed FOSB fusions with a novel partner gene ACTB. In both ACTB::FOSB fusion positive  pseudomyogenic hemangioendothelioma cases the ACTB exon 3 was joined with the FOSB exon 2. The FOSB breakpoint in the ACTB::FOSB fusion matched previously reported breakpoints. This study further confirms specific association between FOSB fusions and  pseudomyogenic hemangioendothelioma.

source.title: Diagnosis of known sarcoma fusions and novel fusion partners by targeted RNA sequencing with identification of a recurrent ACTB-FOSB fusion in pseudomyogenic hemangioendothelioma.

description:
This is part of a multi-centred, randomised, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial, CHOICE-01, that examined therapeutic response to first-line chemotherapy plus PD-1 inhibitor in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients to explore ctDNA-based stratification strategies.

405 treatment-naïve patients with either locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC that do not carry EGFR or ALK driver mutations were randomly assigned to receive toripalimab (n=309) or placebo (n = 156) in combination with chemotherapy. 371 of the 405 patients with pre-treatment ctDNA present (maximal somatic allele frequency of >=0.5%). Blood-based TMB (bTMB) measured by the 520-gene OncoCompass Plus panel (Burning Rock Biotech) was calculated as the number of small single-nucleotide variations (SNVs) and indels detected at an allele frequency of >=0.2% per Mb of coding regions of target genes (1.003 Mb for the panel used). 

Using 13 mutations/ Mb (top 20%) as the cut off, patients with high bTMB achieved greater progression free survival from chemotherapy plus PD-1 inhibitor compare dot the bTMB-low group (interaction p = 0.027). However, no difference in overall survival benefits from the addition of PD-1 inhibitor was observed between the two groups.
name: EID12798

source.title: Circulating tumor DNA-based stratification strategy for chemotherapy plus PD-1 inhibitor in advanced non-small-cell lung cancer.

description:
This is part of a open-label phase 3 trial, NEPTUNE, that examined therapeutic response to first-line durvalumab plus tremelimumab in patients with metastatic non-small cel lung cancer (NSCLC). 823 patiehts with metastatic NSCLC that do not carry EGFR or ALK driver mutations were randomly assigned to receive first-line durvalumab (20 mg/kg every 4 weeks until progression) plus tremelimumab (1 mg/kg every 4 weeks for up to four doses) or standard platinum-based chemotherapy. 

Blood-based TMB (bTMB) was evaluated in 512 patients.bTMB measured by the 500 gene Guardant OMNI plasma next-generation sequencing (NGS) platform was calculated as the number of synonymous and non-synonymous small single-nucleotide variations (SNVs) and short indels detected at all allele fractions per Mb of coding regions of target genes. Among the bTMB-high patients (>= 20 mut/ Mb) (n = 129), no statistically significant overall survival (OS) (HR 0.71 [95% CI: 0.49–1.05]; median OS, 11.7 versus 9.1 months) or progression free survival (PFS) (HR 0.77 [95% CI: 0.51–1.15]) improvement was observed with durvalumab plus tremelimumab (n = 69) compared to chemotherapy (n = 60). In the exploratory analysis of bTMB with various cutoffs (8-28 mut/Mb), OS and PFS analysis demonstrated an association between higher bTMB and improved hazard ratios for durvalumab plus tremelimumab compared to chemotherapy. 

Tissue TMB (tTMB) was also evaluated in 369 of the patients. tTMB measured by the 324 gene FoundationOne CDx platform was calculated as the number of synonymous and non-synonymous small single-nucleotide variations (SNVs) and short indels per Mb of coding regions of target genes. In the exploratory analysis of tTMB with various cutoffs (4-18 mut/Mb), OS and PFS analysis demonstrated an association between higher bTMB and improved hazard ratios for durvalumab plus tremelimumab compared to chemotherapy. Among the 236 patients with matched plasma and tissue samples, moderate correlation was observed between bTMB and tTMB (Spearman’s rho = 0.64; Pearson’sr  =  0.80).

In conclusion, this study did not meet its primary end point of statistically significant improved OS with durvalumab plus tremelimumab compared to chemotherapy among bTMB-high mNSCLC patients. The authors noted that despite this study being limited by altered study design and therefore a small size of the primary analysis population, the therapeutic activity was consistent with observations in previous studies and aligned with expected outcomes based on underlying biological mechanisms.
name: EID12799

source.title: NEPTUNE: Phase 3 Study of First-Line Durvalumab Plus Tremelimumab in Patients With Metastatic NSCLC.

description: In a study of 100 patients with sporadic medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC), RET gene exons 10-11 and 13-16 were analyzed with tumor and matched normal samples. A somatic RET mutation was identified in 43% of cases and of these 79% (34/43) were M918T mutations.
name: EID12800

source.title: Prognostic significance of somatic RET oncogene mutations in sporadic medullary thyroid cancer: a 10-year follow-up study.

description: In this 2017 study, the authors characterized 284 cases of Philadelphia chromosome-like acute lymphoblastic leukemia (Ph-like ALL) identified from a cohort of 1,389 pediatric patients with high-risk B-ALL. This subtype is defined by a gene expression profile similar to BCR::ABL1-positive ALL but lacks that canonical fusion, and is associated with a diverse array of genetic alterations activating cytokine receptor and tyrosine kinase signaling. The cohort showed a male predominance (57.4%) and was enriched for older age and high white blood cell counts. Comprehensive molecular profiling, including reverse transcriptase PCR and transcriptome sequencing, identified targetable kinase alterations in 83.8% of the Ph-like ALL cases. Among these, fusions involving the LYN kinase gene were identified as rare, recurrent oncogenic drivers within this high-risk subtype. The study reported one case harboring a novel GATAD2A::LYN fusion. This fusion retains the tyrosine kinase domain of LYN and is predicted to activate SRC-family kinase signaling. The expression profile of this LYN-fusion-positive case was classified as Ph-like, definitively supporting its biological and diagnostic classification within the BCR::ABL1-like disease spectrum.
name: EID12801

source.title: Targetable kinase gene fusions in high-risk B-ALL: a study from the Children's Oncology Group.

description: This retrospective Japanese multicenter study investigated kinase-activating gene fusions in pediatric B-lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) lacking recurrent cytogenetic abnormalities, with the goal of defining their clinical and biological significance. Among 373 children and adolescents (median age 8.8 years; range 1.9–16 years) analyzed using mRNA sequencing and/or multiplex RT-PCR, 29 patients were identified with kinase or cytokine receptor fusions involving CRLF2 (n=14), PDGFRB (n=8), ABL1 (n=3), JAK2 (n=2), EPOR (n=3), and LYN (n=1).  There was only one fusion involving the LYN kinase gene, indicating LYN fusions as rare oncogenic drivers in pediatric B-ALL. The 5' partner for the LYN fusion was the NCOR1 gene,  and the gene expression profile of the NCOR1::LYN positive case resembled BCR::ABL1–positive ALL, supporting its classification within the Ph-like ALL spectrum. The studied patients showed characteristic high-risk features, including male predominance, older age at diagnosis, high white blood cell counts, and enrichment for NCI high-risk disease, as well as a high frequency of IKZF1 deletions (~73%). Clinically, outcomes were poor with conventional therapy alone, with 5-year event-free and overall survival rates of 48.6% and 73.5%, respectively, and inferior survival compared with fusion-negative cases in the mRNA-seq cohort. The study supports that B-ALLs with fusions involving the LYN kinase gene are associated with the BCR::ABL1 like subtype of the disease.
name: EID12802

source.title: Characterization of pediatric Philadelphia-negative B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia with kinase fusions in Japan.

description: In this 2022 study, the authors investigate the oncogenic role of the MYB::TYK2 fusion gene in high-risk B-lymphoblastic leukemia (HR B-ALL). TYK2 rearrangements are identified as recurrent events in the high-risk BCR::ABL1-like (Ph-like) ALL subtype. The study functionally characterizes the MYB::TYK2 fusion, which was initially isolated from a patient with this aggressive leukemia. Through in vitro and in vivo modeling, the authors demonstrate that the MYB::TYK2 fusion is a driver oncogene that confers cytokine-independent growth in vitro and leads to the development of B-ALL in mice . The authors propose that TYK2 fusions share  similar breakpoints and likely lead to constitutive TYK activation by disrupting its auto-inhibitory domain. Importantly, the study shows that the MYB::TYK2 fusion constitutively activates the JAK/STAT signaling pathway in the studied model systems, consistent with its association with the BCR::ABL1-like (Ph-like) ALL subtype.
name: EID12803

source.title: Exploring the oncogenic and therapeutic target potential of the MYB-TYK2 fusion gene in B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia.

description: RET is a known oncogene that encodes a receptor tyrosine kinase with important roles in cell growth, differentiation, and survival. Germline M918T is strongly linked with multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2B (MEN 2B) and its associated medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC). Somatic M918T is strongly associated with sporadic MTC. This study sought to elucidate the functional mechanisms and molecular properties of M918T RET protein. Isothermal titration calorimetry showed that M918T had >10-fold greater affinity for ATP compared to wildtype. Stoichiometry calculations and analytic gel filtration also suggest that M918T molecules are more likely to form dimers that associate with two ATP molecules compared to the single binding site for wild-type. In vitro kinase assays suggest that M918T increased stability of enzyme-ATP complex, strengthening ATP-binding, and achieving increased kinase activity at lower ATP concentrations compared to wildtype. Immunoprecipitation and western blotting experiments showed that M918T was more highly auto-phosphorylated in the presence or absence of ligand stimulation. Differential scanning calorimetry suggested that M918T may have changes in intramolecular interactions and reduced conformational rigidity that might play a significant role in M918T protein function. In low-stringency nonreducing conditions they show that M918T RET can dimerize and become autophosphorylated even in the absence of ligand stimulation. Taken together, these experiments and others suggest multiple distinct but complementary molecular mechanisms by which M918T leads to functional activation of RET relative to wild-type.
name: EID12805

source.title: Molecular mechanisms of RET receptor-mediated oncogenesis in multiple endocrine neoplasia 2B.

description:
In an open-label, multicenter, multicohort phase 1–2 study of non-small cell lung carcinoma (NCT05099172; total n = 209), single-agent sevabertinib 20 mg BID demonstrated clinically meaningful activity in ERBB2 (HER2)–mutant disease. This population predominantly involves HER2 tyrosine kinase domain (TKD) mutations (90–97% across cohorts), including exon 20 insertion - Y772_A775dupYVMA (60–79%). Confirmed ORR was 64% (95% CI 53 - 75; n = 81; CR 2%, PR 62%, SD 25%) in previously treated patients without prior HER2-targeted therapy, 38% (95% CI 25 - 52; n = 55; CR 5%, PR 33%, SD 42%) in patients previously treated with HER2-directed ADCs, and 71% (95% CI 59 - 81; n = 73; CR 4%, PR 67%, SD 22%) in treatment-naive locally advanced or metastatic disease. Corresponding mPFS 8.3 mo (95% CI 6.9 - 12.3), 5.5 mo (95% CI 4.3 - 8.3), and NE (95% CI 9.6 - NE), and mDoR 9.2 mo (95% CI 6.3 - 13.5), 8.5 mo (95% CI 5.6 - 16.4), and 11.0 mo (95% CI 8.1 -NE), respectively.

Exploratory analyses showed higher response and longer PFS in HER2 TKD mutations vs non-TKD alterations (n = 73 vs 7), with ORR 70% (95% CI 58 - 80) vs 14% (95% CI <1 - 58) and mPFS 9.6 mo (95% CI 6.9 - 12.3) vs 6.9 mo (95% CI 2.5 - NE). In Y772_A775dupYVMA vs other HER2 TKD variants (n = 49 vs 23), with ORR 78% (95% CI 63 - 88) vs 57% (95% CI 35 - 77) and mPFS 12.2 mo (95% CI 6.9 - 16.4) vs 7.0 mo (95% CI 4.0 - NE). These findings support ERBB2 (HER2) mutation, particularly TKD exon 20 insertions, as predictive of response to sevabertinib.

description: In this 2020 case report, the authors present a pediatric patient with relapsed B-lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL), providing critical evidence for the diagnostic and therapeutic role of LYN fusions. The patient was a 6-year-old male who presented with high-risk features, including an initial white blood cell count of 883 × 10⁹/L and a relapsed disease that was refractory to re-induction chemotherapy. Comprehensive molecular diagnostics performed at relapse, including karyotyping and FISH, identified a balanced t(8;17)(q12;p11.2) translocation, which was subsequently confirmed by sequencing to generate an in-frame NCOR1::LYN fusion gene. This fusion joined exon 34 of NCOR1 to exon 8 of LYN, retaining the intact tyrosine kinase domain. Additional high-risk genetic lesions, including deletions of IKZF1 and CDKN2A, were also present. Upon identification of this ABL/SRC-family kinase fusion, the patient was treated with the tyrosine kinase inhibitor dasatinib (60 mg/m²/day) as monotherapy, achieving a complete morphologic and molecular remission within two weeks. This rapid response provided the first direct clinical evidence that leukemias driven by LYN fusions are exquisitely sensitive to dasatinib. The patient subsequently underwent haploidentical stem cell transplantation and remained in minimal residual disease-negative remission on dasatinib maintenance. The authors concluded that the NCOR1::LYN fusion is a recurrent, targetable oncogenic driver in high-risk pediatric B-ALL. Response of the described leukemia to treatment with a kinase inhibitor supports association of the NCOR1::LYN fusion with  the Philadelphia chromosome-like (BCR::ABL1-like) subtype, in which activated kinase signaling is the defining molecular feature.
name: EID12809

source.title: Rapid Molecular Response to Dasatinib in a Pediatric Relapsed Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia With NCOR1-LYN Fusion.

description: In this 2014 genomic profiling study of 1,725 patients with precursor B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL), the authors define the high-risk "Philadelphia chromosome-like" (Ph-like or BCR::ABL1-like) subgroup. This subgroup is characterized by a gene expression profile similar to BCR::ABL1-positive ALL, a high frequency of IKZF1 alterations, and a diverse spectrum of genetic alterations that constitutively activate kinase and cytokine receptor signaling pathways. The cohort included children, adolescents, and young adults up to age 39. RNA sequencing was performed on 136 patients with Ph-like ALL. The study identified kinase-activating alterations in 91% of Ph-like ALL cases. Among these, a novel MYB::TYK2 fusion was identified in one patient. The fusion retained an intact tyrosine kinase domain, and its identification classified this patient's leukemia within the "other JAK-STAT" activating alteration subgroup of Ph-like ALL. The authors concluded that Ph-like ALL is a common, high-risk subtype characterized by a range of genomic alterations activating a limited set of signaling pathways, nearly all of which are potentially amenable to inhibition with approved tyrosine kinase inhibitors. They propose that identifying these alterations, including rare fusions like MYB::TYK2, is critical for directing targeted therapy to improve patient outcomes.
name: EID12810

source.title: Targetable kinase-activating lesions in Ph-like acute lymphoblastic leukemia.

description: In this 2023 study, the authors evaluated the diagnostic utility of NR4A3 immunohistochemistry in acinic cell carcinoma (AciCC) of the salivary gland. The cohort included 128 AciCCs, comprising 85 classic low-grade, 36 with high-grade transformation (HGT), and 7 high-grade tumors. NR4A3 rearrangements were assessed using a custom dual-color break-apart FISH probe. NR4A3 immunoreactivity was observed in 105 of 128 cases (82%), with similar positivity rates across low-grade, HGT, and high-grade AciCCs (82%, 81%, and 86%, respectively). FISH analysis was performed in 57 cases, confirming NR4A3 rearrangements in 23 of 28 (82%) low-grade cases, 11 of 14 (79%) HGT cases, and 2 of 2 (100%) high-grade cases, resulting in an overall confirmation rate of 36 of 44 (82%) in analyzable immunopositive tumors. Eight immunopositive cases (18%) were FISH-negative, while among 10 immunonegative cases, 2 of 8 analyzable tumors (25%) demonstrated NR4A3 rearrangement. Five cases were not evaluable by FISH. The authors conclude that NR4A3 rearrangements are strongly associated with AciCC and that NR4A3 immunohistochemistry is a robust and reliable tool for the differential diagnosis of this tumor.
name: EID12816

source.title: A minority of cases of acinic cell carcinoma of the salivary glands are driven by an NR4A2 rearrangement: the diagnostic utility of the assessment of NR4A2 and NR4A3 alterations in salivary gland tumors.

description:
The MYSTIC study compared response rates for immunotherapy verses chemotherapy. Specifically looking at the efficacy of the anti-PD-L1 therapy, durvalumab, with/without the anti-CTLA-4 therapy, tremelimumab, compared to platinum-based chemotherapy for overall survival (OS) and progress free survival (PFS). When considering implementation of immunotherapy (immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs)), there is a strong correlation between tumors that have high tumor mutational burden (TMB) and success of ICI. Tumor mutational burden can be calculated from both tumor sample (tTMB) and circulating tumor DNA that has been shed and is now collected in the blood (bTMB). This study showed that bTMB, which is less invasive and captures more of the tumor mutational heterogeneity, can be used for determining whether patients should use ICIs in the setting of metastatic NSCLC.
From MYSTIC phase III trial, 1001 of the 1118 patients had adequate plasma samples available and of those, 809 samples had valid bTMB score (meaning above the variant allele frequency (VAF) needed for NGS assays; 809/1001 = 81%). Of those 809 patients, 735 of them had tumor samples available, however 275 samples did not meet criteria for “valid” tTMB due to insufficient tumor sample, insufficient DNA yield, or insufficient VAF to calculate TMB. Ultimately TMB scores from blood were more likely to be valid as compared to TMB scores from tumors. When comparing the shared mutations from matched tumor and blood sequencing assays, across a shared DNA region, 50% of mutations detected were found both in the blood and tumor samples. Furthermore, when matching the tumor and plasma samples, there was a positive correlation between the bTMB and tTMB. When comparing the discordance between bTMB and tTMB, multiple factors should be considered including assay-specific differences in genes tested and TMB algorithms, as well as sample differences, such as the intratumoral heterogeneity common in NSCLC. When considering bTMB scores in clinical outcomes, having greater than 20 mutations per megabase (mut/Mb) had the most favorable OS and PFS when treated with durvalumab plus tremelimumab compared to chemotherapy.
name: EID12822

source.title: A Blood-based Assay for Assessment of Tumor Mutational Burden in First-line Metastatic NSCLC Treatment: Results from the MYSTIC Study.

description: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have been revolutionary in treating solid cancers, however the responses to these therapies can be quite variable. Though response rate to these immunotherapies is often correlated with tumor mutational burden (TMB), this might not be true across all cancer types. Within gastrointestinal tumors, the majority are microsatellite stable (MSS) which has mixed efficacy when treated with ICI compared to microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) gastrointestinal tumors that respond well to ICIs. Previous studies were unsuccessful in showing a correlation between tumor mutational burden (TMB) status and MSS for predicting clinical response to ICI. This study found that the combination of TMB-H status with mutations in specific genes had increased response to ICIs, likely due to the quality of the neoantigens presented in these tumors. 48,606 samples with confirmed gastrointestinal cancer were binned into three groups 1) MSS-TMB-H (3.29%) 2) dMMR/MSI-H (4.67%) and 3) MSS-TMB-L (92.03%). These samples were sequenced using either NextSeq or NovaSeq, which used NGS for 592 or 700 genes respectively. Tumors were considered TMB-H if they had greater than or equal to 10 mutations per megabase (mut/Mb). Within the sequence analysis for the TMB-H/MSI-H groups, a subset of genes had a positive association with antitumor response, these genes are referred to as the modified TMB (mTMB) signature genes (CDC73, CTNNA1, ERBB4, EZH2, JAK2, MAP2K1, MAP2K4, PIK3R1, POLE, PPP2R1A, PPP2R2A, PTPN11, RAF1, RUNX1, STAG2 , and XPO1).  Furthermore, within the MSS-TMB-H group, there was a significantly higher rate of amplification of CCND1 and FGF genes, most of which are located on 11q13. MSS tumors with a mutation in the mTMB genes had distinctive molecular profiles (high mutation counts, indels, SNVs) and immune response indicators (neoantigens and B-cell receptor richness, higher IFN gamma signatures, higher infiltration of NK cells, M1-like macrophages, and Th1 cells, but lower infiltration of M2-like macrophages). Patients with mTMB mutations treated with ICIs had longer overall survival compared to mTMB wildtype patients treated with ICIs within the CARIS and MSKCC cohorts. Importantly, for patients that did not receive ICIs, there was no difference between the OS and mTMB gene signature.
name: EID12823

source.title: Mutational analysis of microsatellite-stable gastrointestinal cancer with high tumour mutational burden: a retrospective cohort study.

description: This study presented clinicopathological and molecular findings of TFCP2-rearranged rhabdomyosarcomas with epithelioid and/or spindle cell morphology. The cohort comprised 14 cases, including 3 index cases published in 2018. Six males and 8 females were included, with an age range of 11-86 years at diagnosis (mean: 31 years). Tumors were located in the bones (n=12/14) or soft tissue (n=2/14). TFCP2 gene fusions from FFPE materials were identified by RNA-seq (n=10/10) or anchored multiplex PCR (n=4/4), showing that exons 5 or 6 of FUS (n=8) or EWSR1 (n=6) were fused to exon 2 of TFCP2. FISH analyses were performed in select cases using EWSR1, FUS, and TFCP2 break-apart probes, showing positivity in 2 of 3, 5 of 5, and 9 of 9 tested cases, respectively. Homozygous deletion of CDKN2A was detected by aCGH in all tested cases (n=9/9), and mutations in the exon 1 of MYOD1 were absent (DNA, n=0/8; RNA, n=0/10) by Sanger sequencing. ALK overexpression was found in most cases (n=11/14) without underlying ALK fusion identified by either break-apart FISH (n=0/5) or NGS (n=0/14). Seven EWSR1/FUS::TFCP2 cases were subjected to unsupervised consensus clustering analyses, showing distinct segregation from the other rhabdomyosarcomas that include embryonal rhabdomyosarcomas (n=6), alveolar rhabdomyosarcomas (n=8), MYOD1-mutated rhabdomyosarcomas (n=4), and VGLL2-fused rhabdomyosarcomas (n=5). Collectively, this study showed that TFCP2-rearranged rhabdomyosarcomas exhibit recurrent EWSR1/FUS::TFCP2 gene fusions and are distinct from other rhabdomyosarcoma subtypes.
name: EID12825

source.title: A subset of epithelioid and spindle cell rhabdomyosarcomas is associated with TFCP2 fusions and common ALK upregulation.

description: This study presented clinicopathological and molecular features of 11 cases of head and neck rhabdomyosarcomas (HNRMSs). The median age of the cohort was 29 years, ranging 16-74 years with no sex bias. All cases but one were intraosseous, involving the mandible (n=4), maxilla (n=3), and skull (n=3). The remaining case occurred in the superficial cervical soft tissue. Molecularly, FUS::TFCP2 (n=7) and EWSR1::TFCP2 (n=4) gene fusions were identified by FISH analyses and/or targeted DNA/RNA sequencing. ALK expression was detected in most cases by IHC (n=9/10), with an intragenic deletion identified in 43% of tested cases (n=3/7). CDKN2A loss was identified in all 5 tested cases. The lesions displayed characteristic spindle and epithelioid morphology. The authors also performed a literature review and included 27 TFCP2-rearranged HNRMS cases, showing that this disease mostly affects young adults and pediatric patients. In summary, HNRMSs with spindle cell and epitheloid phenotype exhibit recurrent EWSR1/FUS::TFCP2 gene fusions and preferentially arise in the skeleton.
name: EID12826

source.title: Head and neck rhabdomyosarcoma with TFCP2 fusions and ALK overexpression: a clinicopathological and molecular analysis of 11 cases.

description: This study reported clinicopathologic and molecular features of 25 cases of fusion-driven spindle cell/sclerosing rhabdomyosarcoma (SCSRMS). The tumors occurred in bone (n=19) and soft tissue (n=6). The bone tumor cohort included 6 male and 13 female patients, with an age range of 13-74 years (median age: 41 years), whereas the soft tissue tumors occurred in 4 men and 2 women, with an age range of 28-71 years (median age: 50 years ). In bone tumor cases, 17 of 19 cases were analyzed by NGS with the remaining 2 cases only studied by FISH. NGS analyses revealed the following gene fusions: FUS::TFCP2 (n=12/17), EWSR1::TFCP2 (n=3/17), and MEIS1::NCOA2 (n=2/17), with exon breakpoints identified. Specifically, exon 5 of EWSR1 was joined to exon 2 of TFCP2 in all 3 EWSR1::TFCP2 cases. FISH also successfully identified EWSR1 rearrangements (n=2/2). Among the studied soft tissue tumor cases 1 of 6 showed exon 5 of EWSR1 fused to exon 2 of TFCP2 by NGS, whereas the remaining 5 cases exhibited non-TFCP2 gene fusions. The study  confirms EWSR1::TFCP2 as one of the primary oncogenic drivers in bone and soft tissue SCSRMS.
name: EID12827

source.title: Fusion-driven Spindle Cell Rhabdomyosarcomas of Bone and Soft Tissue: A Clinicopathologic and Molecular Genetic Study of 25 Cases.

description: In this 2019 study, the authors aimed to evaluate the usefulness of NR4A3 immunostaining and compare it with NR4A3 Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) for the differential diagnosis of acinic cell carcinoma (AciCC). The study included 64 AciCC cases (53 low-grade tumors and 11 with high-grade transformation), 29 mammary analogue secretory carcinoma (MASC), and 70 other salivary gland carcinomas, evaluated by NR4A3 immunostaining. NR4A3 immunostaining was considered positive when moderate to strong nuclear staining was observed, while cytoplasmic staining was regarded as nonspecific. Moderate to strong nuclear NR4A3 expression was detected in 63 of 64 AciCCs (98%), including all high-grade transformed cases; only one case was negative. In contrast, none of the MASCs or other salivary gland carcinomas showed nuclear NR4A3 staining. These findings confirmed specific association of the NR4A3 rearrangement and upregulation with AciCC. FISH analysis was successfully performed in 58 AciCCs, of which 49 cases (84%) showed abnormal NR4A3 signals consistent with gene translocation (44 with split signals and 5 with single red signals). Nine cases (16%) showed normal FISH results. Samples were classified as positive when more than 20% of 50 counted nuclei displayed abnormal signals. The authors concluded that NR4A3 rearrangement is highly associated with AciCC and the immunostaining is sensitive and specific marker for AciCC, including high-grade cases. The studies shows utility of confirming NR4A3 rearrangement by immunostaining and FISH in distinguishing AciCC from MASC.
name: EID12828

source.title: Nuclear NR4A3 Immunostaining Is a Specific and Sensitive Novel Marker for Acinic Cell Carcinoma of the Salivary Glands.

description:
In this 2018 study by Keiko Segawa et al., the authors analyzed 22 tumors, including 16 clear cell sarcomas of soft tissue (CCSST) and 6 clear cell sarcoma–like gastrointestinal tumors (CCSLGT), to characterize EWSR1-related gene rearrangements using FISH and RT-PCR.
EWSR1 rearrangement was identified in 93.8% (15/16) of CCSSTs and 66.7% (4/6) of CCSLGTs. In CCSST, 68.8% of cases showed concurrent ATF1 rearrangement, supporting the presence of the EWSR1::ATF1 fusion as the predominant genetic alteration; this was confirmed by RT-PCR in tested cases. In contrast, CCSLGT demonstrated a more heterogeneous fusion pattern, with both EWSR1::ATF1 and EWSR1::CREB1 detected (each in 33.3% of cases). Rare CREM rearrangements were also observed in both tumor types.
Overall, the study reinforces the strong association of EWSR1::ATF1 fusion with clear cell sarcoma of soft tissue, while EWSR1::CREB1 appears relatively more frequent in gastrointestinal counterparts, highlighting the diagnostic utility of identifying specific EWSR1 fusion partners in distinguishing these related entities.
name: EID12829

source.title: Detection of specific gene rearrangements by fluorescence in situ hybridization in 16 cases of clear cell sarcoma of soft tissue and 6 cases of clear cell sarcoma-like gastrointestinal tumor.

description:
In this 2002 study by Cristina R Antonescu et al., 12 histologically confirmed cases of clear cell sarcoma (CCS) arising in the deep soft tissues of the extremities were analyzed to assess the prevalence and diagnostic utility of the EWSR1::ATF1 fusion using RT-PCR on both frozen and formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue.
Histologically, 10 of 12 cases exhibited the classic nested epithelioid morphology with clear to pale eosinophilic cytoplasm, central nuclei, and prominent nucleoli. Immunohistochemistry showed diffuse positivity for HMB45 and MITF in all cases, and S-100 in 10 cases, supporting melanocytic differentiation. Ultrastructural analysis revealed melanosomes in 6 of 7 examined tumors.
Molecular analysis detected the EWSR1::ATF1 fusion transcript in 11 of 12 cases (91%), all demonstrating the in-frame fusion of EWSR1 exon 8 to ATF1 codon 65, with no variant structures identified. RT-PCR for MITF transcripts confirmed expression of the melanocyte-specific MITF-M isoform in all tested cases.
These findings establish EWSR1::ATF1 as a highly sensitive and recurrent molecular marker for CCS. Its detection serves as a reliable diagnostic tool, differentiating CCS from morphologic mimics such as malignant melanoma, and confirms CCS as a genetically defined, melanocytic sarcoma driven by this characteristic fusion.
name: EID12830

source.title: Molecular diagnosis of clear cell sarcoma: detection of EWS-ATF1 and MITF-M transcripts and histopathological and ultrastructural analysis of 12 cases.

description: The PAX5::AUTS2 represents a rare primary oncogenic driver in  B-lymphoblastic Leukemia/lymphoma (B-ALL). An international cohort of 50 patients—including 16 previously reported cases—was assembled, with fusion status confirmed or predicted through a combination of conventional karyotyping, fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), SNP array analysis, optical genome mapping (OGM), RT PCR, whole genome sequencing, and whole exome sequencing. Cohort analyses consistently demonstrate that PAX5::AUTS2 is associated with high relapse rates, frequent central nervous system involvement, and poor event-free and overall survival, with particularly adverse outcomes observed in very young children. The study reported a 5-year cumulative incidence of relapse of approximately 48% and an event-free survival of roughly 48%, highlighting a prognosis inferior to most standard-risk B ALL groups. Infants and toddlers (<3 years) comprise the majority of cases and are most vulnerable. Collectively, these findings support the PAX5::AUTS2 as a primary driver in B-ALL in high-risk disease.
name: EID12838

source.title: PAX5::AUTS2 childhood B-ALL: a relapse-prone genetic subtype with frequent central nervous system involvement and a poor outcome.

description:
The transmembrane domain mutation G380R was tested in a series of assays for an evaluation of oncogenicity. 

G380R was stably transfected into 3T3 cells along with WT controls.
TAS (Transformation Activity Score) was defined by logistic regression of four experimental batches of focus formation assays and four experimental batches of the low-serum cell proliferation assays using these cells, into a score of 1 to 4.

G380R had a TAS score of 3.

In parallel, mixed-all-nominated-in-one (MANO) method was used for evaluation of transforming potential. Barcoded G380R and other barcoded variants were stably transfected into 3T3 cells along with controls and grown together. Next generation sequencing was used to compare relative amounts of different barcodes for a measure of relative proliferation. 

Using this method, G380R had approximately 6 fold change compared to WT on a base 2 scale (~ 64 fold).

The authors evaluated this result as

oncogenic: higher TAS score and significantly faster growth compared with WT
name: EID12847

source.title: Comprehensive functional evaluation of variants of fibroblast growth factor receptor genes in cancer.

description:
The tyrosine kinase domain mutation G697C in FGFR3 was tested in a series of assays for an evaluation of oncogenicity. 

G697C was stably transfected into 3T3 cells along with WT controls.
TAS (Transformation Activity Score) was defined by logistic regression of four experimental batches of focus formation assays and four experimental batches of the low-serum cell proliferation assays using these cells, into a score of 1 to 4.

G697C had a TAS score of 1.

In parallel, mixed-all-nominated-in-one (MANO) method was used for evaluation of transforming potential. Barcoded G697C and other barcoded variants were stably transfected into 3T3 cells along with controls and grown together. Next generation sequencing was used to compare relative amounts of different barcodes for a measure of relative proliferation. 

Using this method, G697C had approximately 1 fold change compared to WT on a base 2 scale (~ 2 fold).

The authors evaluated this result as

neutral, which was a category having neither higher or lower TAS score and neither significantly faster or slower growth compared to WT.
