source.title: Comprehensive functional evaluation of variants of fibroblast growth factor receptor genes in cancer.

description:
This retrospective analysis of the Phase 3 EAGLE trial (NCT02369874) evaluated tissue tumor mutational burden (tTMB) and blood TMB (bTMB) as predictive biomarkers in platinum-refractory recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). Using WES, tTMB (n=153) was calculated from somatic SNVs and indels (<20,bp) at 5–80% allele frequency. bTMB (n=247) was determined using the GuardantOMNI assay (500 genes; 2,Mb), incorporating variants across all allele frequencies.

In the tissue-evaluable cohort, cutoffs from 10 to 20 mut/Mb were assessed. For durvalumab monotherapy, a 10 mut/Mb threshold showed the best discrimination [HR: 0.72 (CI: 0.45–1.15)], though OS differences were not significant. For durvalumab plus tremelimumab, significant OS benefit was observed at 10 [HR: 0.52 (CI: 0.28–0.98)] and 12 mut/Mb [HR: 0.46 (CI: 0.24–0.86)] cutoffs. At 10 mut/Mb, median OS for high- vs. low-tTMB was 9.9 vs. 4.4 months (durvalumab) and 16.0 vs. 3.3 months (combination).

In the blood-evaluable cohort, bTMB ≥ 16mut/Mb was the optimal predictive threshold. Patients with bTMB ≥ 16 achieved superior survival over chemotherapy for both durvalumab (OS HR: 0.39; PFS HR: 0.48) and combination therapy (OS HR: 0.38; PFS HR: 0.45). Median OS for bTMB ≥ 16 was 8.1 (durvalumab) and 7.6 (combination) vs. 4.0 months (SoC); benefits were absent in patients with bTMB < 16. These findings suggest tTMB ≥ 10 and bTMB ≥16 mut/Mb as robust predictive thresholds for identifying HNSCC patients benefiting from checkpoint inhibition.

disease.name: Head And Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma

name: EID12850

source.title: Tumor Mutational Burden as a Predictor of Survival with Durvalumab and/or Tremelimumab Treatment in Recurrent or Metastatic Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma.

description: This analysis of the Phase 2 KEYNOTE-782 trial (NCT03664024) evaluated the correlation of blood tumor mutational burden (bTMB) with the efficacy of first-line pembrolizumab plus platinum-based chemotherapy in patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The cfDNA assay utilized was GRAIL, comprising 654 genes (1.9 Mb). Paired white blood cells were sequenced to eliminate mutations related to clonal hematopoiesis and germline variants. bTMB was calculated as the total number of nonsynonymous mutations per megabase pair of the sequenced genome. In the bTMB-evaluable population (n=101), the distribution of bTMB scores was found to be similar among both responders and non-responders. Consequently, the study concluded that bTMB does not have predictive value for the efficacy of pembrolizumab combined with platinum-based chemotherapy in this clinical setting.
name: EID12851

source.title: Blood tumor mutational burden and response to pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy in non-small cell lung cancer: KEYNOTE-782.

description: In this study, the authors analyzed 14 cases of angiomatoid fibrous histiocytoma (AFH). The EWSR1::CREB1 fusion associated with t(2;22)(q33;q12) was detected in 13 of 14 tumors by dual‑color and four‑color FISH, demonstrating rearrangement of the EWSR1 and CREB1 loci. In the case with available frozen tissue, RT‑PCR confirmed an in‑frame EWSR1::CREB1 transcript. Sequencing studies indicate that the fusion typically joins the EWSR1 N‑terminal activation domain (commonly exon 7) to the CREB1 bZIP DNA‑binding region (commonly exon 7), generating an intact chimeric transcription factor that drives aberrant CREB‑mediated transcription. Although exon‑specific breakpoints were not detailed in this study, the RT‑PCR–verified transcript is consistent with the canonical EWSR1‑exon‑7::CREB1‑exon‑7 configuration described in AFH. These findings establish EWSR1::CREB1 as a highly specific diagnostic biomarker that helps distinguish AFH from clear cell sarcoma and other histologic mimics with alternative EWSR1 fusion partners.
name: EID12852

source.title: EWSR1-CREB1 and EWSR1-ATF1 fusion genes in angiomatoid fibrous histiocytoma.

description: In this study, the authors report a 34‑year-old patient with angiomatoid fibrous histiocytoma (AFH) who initially presented with a pulmonary nodule and a 4th‑rib lesion and subsequently developed metastases to the iliac bone, subcutaneous tissue, pleura, lymph nodes, and brain. FISH confirmed an EWSR1::CREB1 rearrangement, and RNA-based next-generation sequencing identified an in-frame EWSR1 exon 7–CREB1 exon 7 fusion. This molecular finding established the AFH diagnosis across multiple lesions despite the tumor’s atypical and highly metastatic presentation. The disease progressed systemically, resulting in death 18 months after initial surgery, representing the first documented case of fatal, multi-organ metastatic EWSR1::CREB1–positive AFH and highlighting the rare but significant potential for aggressive behavior in tumors harboring this fusion.
name: EID12853

source.title: Angiomatoid fibrous histiocytoma with EWSR1-CREB1 gene fusion occurs in lungs and ribs with systemic multiple metastases: a case report and review of the literature.

description: In this study, the authors analyzed 9 cases of angiomatoid fibrous histiocytoma (AFH). The EWSR1::CREB1 fusion was identified as the predominant molecular alteration, detected in 8 of 9 tumors by RT‑PCR and confirmed by Sanger sequencing, which demonstrated an identical junction of EWSR1 exon 7 fused to CREB1 exon 7 in all positive cases. FISH analysis showed EWSR1 rearrangement in 7 of 8 evaluable tumors, and conventional cytogenetic analysis in one case revealed a t(2;22)(q33;q12) translocation. These complementary molecular techniques establish EWSR1::CREB1 as the most frequent and characteristic fusion in AFH, serving as a highly useful diagnostic marker that distinguishes AFH from other round/spindle cell sarcomas, including Ewing sarcoma and clear cell sarcoma.
name: EID12855

source.title: EWSR1-CREB1 is the predominant gene fusion in angiomatoid fibrous histiocytoma.

description: This landmark study provided revised classification of B-lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) based on integrated genomic findings from 1,988 childhood and adult B-ALLs. All cases were subjected to RNA-seq analysis, and a subset of them were further characterized by WGS (n=17), WES (n=73), and SNP array (n=1,141).  Among 23 described subtypes, two were related to the alterations of B-lineage transcription factor gene PAX5 despite showing different gene expression patterns, and were designated as PAX5alt and PAX5 p.P80R groups. The first group included diverse PAX5 alterations, including gene fusions, non-p.P80R mutations, and/or intrachromosomal focal amplification (PAX5amp). PAX5 fusions were found in 57 cases (38.5% of the PAXalt group); they were in-frame and involved 24 partner genes, the most frequent of which were ETV6 (n=19), NOL4L (n=5), AUTS2 (n=4), and CBFA2T3 (n=4). Importantly, PAX5::JAK2 were observed exclusively in Ph-like B-ALL, and PAX5::ZCCHC7 were observed in B-ALL cases with other subtype-specific pathognomonic events. In summary, PAX5 fusions, except PAX5::JAK2 and PAX5::ZCCHC7, are subtype-defining alterations for the PAX5alt B-ALL.
name: EID12867

source.title: PAX5-driven subtypes of B-progenitor acute lymphoblastic leukemia.

description: This European population-based cohort study examined the genomic landscape of 110 consecutively diagnosed childhood (aged 1-18 years) “B-other” lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) cases, collected over 7 years in the Czech Republic. The B-other ALL was defined as B-ALL negative for ETV6::RUNX1, BCR::ABL1, TCF3::PBX1, KMT2A-rearrangements, hyperdiploidy (>50 chromosomes), and hypodiploidy (<44 chromosomes). Molecular alterations were characterized using a combination of SNP arrays (n=103), WES (n=109), and RNA-seq (n=69) as well as RT-PCR and flow cytometry for select alterations. In-frame PAX5 gene fusions were identified in 14 patients, involving 11 distinct fusion partners. Of those, ten fusion types retained a large 5’ portion of PAX5 (exons 1-5/6/7/8) joined to partner genes. The remaining PAX5::ZCCHC7 fusion (n=2 cases), generated by an intrachromosomal inversion joining PAX5 with its adjacent gene ZCCHC7, resulted in near-complete loss of PAX5. This finding suggests distinct biological characteristics of PAX5::ZCCHC7 in B-ALL leukemogenesis compared to other PAX5 fusions. In summary, PAX5 fusions, except PAX5::ZCCHC7, represent primary oncogenic drivers in 11% (12/110) of B-other ALL.
name: EID12868

source.title: Genomic landscape of pediatric B-other acute lymphoblastic leukemia in a consecutive European cohort.

description: This large FISH-based screening study systematically identified PAX5 fusion partners in a cohort of 446 patients with childhood acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). Interphase FISH was performed on all cases and revealed patterns suggestive of PAX5 rearrangements in 10 cases, corresponding to 2.2% of tested childhood ALLs and 2.6% of B-cell ALLs. Using a combination of RACE (rapid amplification of cDNA ends) with Sanger sequencing and fusion gene-specific RT-PCR, the authors identified PAX5 fusion partners in 9 of 10 cases. In addition to the previously reported PAX5 partners (PML, ETV6, and H20orf112), this study identified five novel gene partners, including transcription regulators (HIPK1 and DACH1), scaffold proteins (POM121C, BRD1), and a kinase (JAK2). The study showed that PAX5 fusions represent important class of primary oncogenic alterations in B-ALL.
name: EID12869

source.title: Incidence and diversity of PAX5 fusion genes in childhood acute lymphoblastic leukemia.

description: In this 2020 study, the authors analyzed clinical, histopathologic, and RNA sequencing data from 37 infants with rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS) diagnosed before six months of age. The median age of the cohort was 2.8 months (range 0–5.8 months). Spindle cell RMS (SRMS) was identified in eight (22%) patients. Among these, VGLL2 fusions were detected in three cases, with NCOA2 (n = 2) or CITED2 (n = 1) as fusion partners. Histologically, these VGLL2-positive tumors displayed a fibromatous-like spindle cell pattern. Fusion-positive SRMS cases were associated with favorable outcomes and long-term survival. Overall, the authors highlighted VGLL2 fusions as a diagnostic biomarker for infantile SRMS, enabling molecular distinction from embryonal and alveolar RMS subtypes.
name: EID12870

source.title: Integrative clinical and biopathology analyses to understand the clinical heterogeneity of infantile rhabdomyosarcoma: A report from the French MMT committee.

description: In this 2021 study, the authors analyzed clinical, pathologic, molecular, and radiologic features of 4 pediatric patients with VGLL2-rearranged infantile sclerosing and spindle-cell rhabdomyosarcoma (ssRMS). Three patients were diagnosed at birth and one at 12 months of age. All primary tumors were localized but considered unresectable, and initial management included chemotherapy or observation. RNA sequencing confirmed VGLL2::NCOA2 or VGLL2::CITED2 fusion transcripts in all cases. Three patients showed high-grade sarcomatous transformation at progression, whereas one retained low-grade morphology in a metastatic adrenal lesion. Metastatic spread occurred in 3 patients (lungs, bone, lymph nodes, adrenal), and 2 patients died of disease. Whole-exome sequencing revealed low mutational burden in primary tumors and increased genomic instability with patient-specific alterations at relapse, including TP53, CDKN2A/B, and FGFR4 mutations. Transcriptomic clustering confirmed that both low- and high-grade tumors retained VGLL2-rearranged RMS signatures. The study highlights that VGLL2-rearranged RMS, although often described as indolent, can progress aggressively, especially when initial surgical resection is not feasible.
name: EID12871

source.title: Infantile Rhabdomyosarcomas With VGLL2 Rearrangement Are Not Always an Indolent Disease: A Study of 4 Aggressive Cases With Clinical, Pathologic, Molecular, and Radiologic Findings.

description: In this 2020 study, the authors analyzed four cases of follicular lymphoma using circulating tumor DNA and droplet digital PCR to monitor EZH2 hotspot mutations, including A682G. One patient with transformed follicular lymphoma carried the EZH2 A682G mutation with a variant allele frequency of 1.8% in a bone marrow biopsy; seven months later, after multiple failed lines of therapy, the mutation was detected concurrently at 38.2% in a lymph node biopsy and 74.0% in circulating tumor DNA shortly before the patient's death. In this patient, the A682G mutation persisted across multiple anatomical sites and coincided with immunochemotherapy resistance, aggressive transformation, and a fatal disease outcome. Furthermore, the patient's EZH2 mutation levels in circulating tumor DNA tracked with tumor burden and PET-CT findings, suggesting that monitoring the persistent A682G mutation may reflect disease progression and treatment failure. The authors note that activating EZH2 mutations, including A682G, are clinically relevant in follicular lymphoma (occurring in ~25% of patients) and suggest they can serve as biomarkers for tumor burden and disease aggressiveness, supporting an oncogenic association of EZH2 A682G in follicular lymphoma.
name: EID12875

source.title: Quantitative Analysis and Monitoring of EZH2 Mutations Using Liquid Biopsy in Follicular Lymphoma.

description: In this 2013 study, the authors analyzed 366 follicular lymphoma (FL) patients with additional paired samples from 33 cases of transformed FL. Patients harbored EZH2 mutations predominantly at codons Y646, A682, and A692, with variant allele frequencies (VAFs) ranging from 2% to 61%. In total, 9 A682G mutations were detected. Comparative analysis with other recurrently mutated genes (CREBBP, MLL2, TNFRSF14, and MEF2B) demonstrated that the majority of EZH2 mutations were clonal. Gene expression analysis of high tumor-content samples identified 106 differentially expressed genes associated with EZH2-mutant cases. The authors conclude that EZH2 mutations act as early events in follicular lymphoma and contribute to disease pathogenesis.
name: EID12876

source.title: EZH2 mutations are frequent and represent an early event in follicular lymphoma.

description:
In a saturation mutagenesis study, all possible point mutations in the FGFR 1-4 kinase domain (amino acids 472-807 for FGFR3) were tested. Lentiviral plasmids were infected at MOI < 0.3 into the growth factor-dependent cell line MCF10A, so that that majority of cells contained no more than one distinct stably transduced FGFR point mutation after selection was performed. 

Cells were then cultured in medium lacking growth factors and with serum reduced to 2% for 17-20 days, and then assayed with next generation sequencing to determine which FGFR constructs were present and enriched. 

All replicates of synonymous mutations were used as control, and activation was calculated as enriched FGFR construct frequency divided by control, then log transformed, and then classified as follows:  

potentially activating (1.5- to 2.5-fold), weakly activating (>2.5- to 5-fold), activating (>5- to 10-fold), strongly activating (>10-fold).

5 percent of activating mutations found were in FGFR3. 

N540K was classified as potentially activating with median activation of 2.0229 and 1.8809 reported for 2 distinct nucleotide changes (C1620A and C1620G).
name: EID12881

source.title: Saturation mutagenesis identifies activating and resistance-inducing FGFR kinase domain mutations.

description: Popovici-Muller et al. reported preliminary efficacy data from an ongoing phase 1 study of ivosidenib (AG-120) monotherapy in patients with IDH1-mutated malignancies. In patients with relapsed or refractory IDH1-mutated  acute myeloid leukemia (AML), interim results demonstrated an overall response rate of 42% and a complete response rate of 22%, with a median duration of complete response of 9.3 months. Ex vivo treatment of primary AML samples harboring IDH1 R132H or IDH1 R132C mutations resulted in potent suppression of 2-hydroxyglutarate (2-HG) production and induction of myeloid differentiation, whereas IDH1 wild-type samples did not demonstrate these effects. These findings support sensitivity of IDH1 R132H- or IDH1 R132C-mutated AML to ivosidenib.
name: EID12903

source.title: Discovery of AG-120 (Ivosidenib): A First-in-Class Mutant IDH1 Inhibitor for the Treatment of IDH1 Mutant Cancers.

description: This is part of a randomised phase 3 trial, CheckpOiNt Blockade For the Inihibition of Relapsed Mesothelioma (CONFIRM), that examined therapeutic response to the anti-PD1 inhibitor, nivolumab, in patients with relapsed mesothelioma. Patients were randomised to receive nivolumab (221 patients, 6 cycles without dose reduction) or placebo (111 patients, 4 cycles). As part of the exploratory multi-omic analysis, tumour mutational burden (TMB) was measured via whole transcriptome sequencing on the archival formalin fixed tumour blocks of a subset of patients who achieved a partial response (R group, n = 12) or no response (NR group, n = 9) to nivolumab. No significant difference in TMB was observed between these two groups of patients (both approximately 5 mutations/ Mb).
name: EID12918

source.title: Constitutive inflammation and epithelial-mesenchymal transition dictate sensitivity to nivolumab in CONFIRM: a placebo-controlled, randomised phase III trial.

description:
This is part of the randomised double-blind phase 3 trial, CameL-sq, a study that assessed the therapeutic effectiveness of the PD-1 blockade, camrelizumab plus chemotherapy as first-line treatment in advanced lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) patients. 389 treatment naïve state IIIB-IV LUSC patients negative of sensitising EGFR or ALK genetic alterations were randomised 1:1 to receive either camrelizumab (200mg) or placebo in combination with chemotherapy (5 mg/mL*min carboplatin and 175 mg/m2 paclitaxel). 

Part of this study explores the value of blood TMB (bTMB) as a predictive biomarker in this setting. For this analysis, baseline tissue and peripheral blood samples were collected prior to initial treatment and an on-treatment peripheral blood sample collected after two cycles of treatment for 270 patients (134 from the combination group, 136 from the chemo only group). Pre-treatment tissue TMB (tTMB), bTMB, and on-treatment bTMB were measured using next-generation sequencing on a pre-designed 543-gene panel. TMB was calculated as the number of nonsynonymous mutations (SNVs and InDels) in coding regions that met a certain sequencing depth (100x for tissue and 500x for plasma) and an allele frequency (5% for tissue and 0.7% for plasma) per Mg of the exonic region. Driver gene mutations and hotspot mutations included in the dbSNP138/COSMIC database were removed from the TMB calculation. The tTMB or bTMB-High groups were defined as those with a TMB value ≥ 75% level. 

Among patients that received the combination treatment, pre-treatment tTMB or bTMB showed no predictive or prognostic value. Conversely, on-treatment bTMB and the bTMB dynamics, measured by ∆bTMB (the difference between on-treatment and pretreatment bTMB levels), showed complementary and non-redundant predictive value for the therapeutic benefit of the combination treatment. Specifically, patients with low on-treatment bTMB achieved longer PFS (median PFS, 9.1 vs 4.1 months; HR = 0.190, P < 0.001) and OS (median, not reached vs 8.0 months; HR = 0.144, P < 0.001). Patients with increased or unchanged bTMB compared to pretreatment (∆bTMB ≥ 0) had shorter PFS (median, 4.5 vs 8.5 months; HR = 2.545, P < 0.001) and OS (median, 9.0 months vs not reached; HR = 4.199, P = 0.201) compared to those with reduced bTMB following treatment (∆bTMB < 0). Patients with low on-treatment bTMB and ∆bTMB < 0 had the longest PFS and OS, while those with high on-treatment bTMB and ∆bTMB ≥ 0 the worst PFS and OS.  Notably, on-treatment bTMB predicts long-term benefit from camrelizumab plus chemotherapy among patients achieving initial radiologic stable disease. Among the 48 patients with initial SD from the combination treatment, those with high on-treatment bTMB had significantly poorer PFS (median, 4.1 vs 5.6 months; HR = 2.861, P = 0.002) and OS (median, 7.8 vs 18.2 months; HR = 3.546, P = 0.001) compared to patients with low on-treatment bTMB.

In conclusion, the combination of on-treatment bTMB and its dynamics is predictive for the therapeutic benefit of camrelizumab in combination with chemotherapy in advanced LUSC patients.
name: EID12919

source.title: On-treatment blood TMB as predictors for camrelizumab plus chemotherapy in advanced lung squamous cell carcinoma: biomarker analysis of a phase III trial.

description: In this study, the authors investigated the role of the EGFR T790M mutation using inducible mouse lung tumor models expressing T790M alone or in combination with the activating L858R mutation. They demonstrated that expression of T790M alone is sufficient to induce lung adenocarcinoma formation in vivo in the absence of additional activating EGFR kinase domain mutations. Importantly, both T790M-only and T790M/L858R tumors were dependent on continued mutant EGFR expression for tumor maintenance and were resistant to the EGFR inhibitor erlotinib. The double mutant exhibited a more aggressive tumor phenotype, with earlier onset, higher tumor burden, and stronger oncogenic signaling compared with T790M alone. These findings demonstrate that EGFR T790M is sufficient to drive lung adenocarcinoma formation in vivo and can further enhance tumorigenicity when combined with activating EGFR mutations such as L858R.
name: EID12925

source.title: Development of new mouse lung tumor models expressing EGFR T790M mutants associated with clinical resistance to kinase inhibitors.

description: The authors performed retrospective analysis of 66 myoepithelial (ME) tumors arising outside the salivary glands, including soft tissue, bone, and visceral lesions. The cohort included 36 females and 30 males, with a wide age range of 1 to 75 years (median 26 years). EWSR1 gene rearrangement was detected by fluorescence in situ hybridization in 30 (45%) cases. More than half of the cases (n=16) occurred in children and young adults (less than 30 years of age). Among cases positive for EWSR1 rearrangement, POU5F1 rearrangement was identified by FISH in 5 tumors (8%), all arising in the deep soft tissues of the extremities, typically showing a clear cell, nested morphology. An PBX1 rearrangement was found in 5 EWSR1 positive tumors, occurring in deep soft tissue, bone, and lung, often displaying bland spindle cell or clear epithelioid morphology. A single ZNF444 rearrangement was observed in an EWSR1 positive tumor occurring in a 64-year-old female in the lung. Tumors without identified fusion partners but harboring EWSR1 rearrangements (n=19) exhibited variable morphologies, including small blue cell, epithelioid, and spindle patterns. EWSR1-negative tumors (n=36, 55%) were more often benign, superficially located, or cutaneous, and sometimes showed ductal or glandular differentiation. Overall, the authors concluded that EWSR1 rearrangement is a common molecular event in ME tumors in soft tissues and is absent in myoepithelial carcinomas of the salivary gland and other related tumors.
name: EID12926

source.title: EWSR1-POU5F1 fusion in soft tissue myoepithelial tumors. A molecular analysis of sixty-six cases, including soft tissue, bone, and visceral lesions, showing common involvement of the EWSR1 gene.

description:
In this 2024 study, the authors analyzed 40 myoepithelial tumors of soft tissue and bone arising in patients ≤21 years of age. The cohort included 22 females and 18 males, with ages ranging from 3 months to 21 years (median 11.5 years). Molecular testing demonstrated evidence of gene fusions in 9 of 21 (43%) tested cases. Rearrangements involving the EWSR1 gene were detected by FISH in 6 of 18 (33%) cases. Among cases analyzed by next-generation sequencing, an EWSR1::POU5F1 fusion was identified in one tumor, while additional non-EWSR1 fusions included FUS::KLF17 and BRD4::CITED1.

Tumors harboring EWSR1 rearrangements did not show a single uniform morphology but were seen across both benign and malignant lesions with variable histologic patterns, including epithelioid, spindle, and mixed cell types in myxoid or chondroid backgrounds. EWSR1-negative tumors comprised a substantial proportion of cases and included tumors lacking both EWSR1 and FUS rearrangements, highlighting genetic heterogeneity in this entity.

Overall, the authors concluded that while EWSR1 rearrangement represents a recurrent and diagnostically useful molecular alteration in a subset of pediatric myoepithelial tumors, it is not universally present, and its absence does not exclude the diagnosis. Therefore, integration of morphology, immunohistochemistry, and molecular testing is required for accurate diagnosis, with EWSR1 fusions serving as supportive but not definitive diagnostic markers.
name: EID12927

source.title: Myoepithelial tumors of soft tissue and bone in children and young adults: A clinicopathologic study of 40 cases occurring in patients ≤ 21 Years of age.

description: In this 2011 study the authors analyzed 18 cutaneous myoepithelial tumors arising in 7 female and 11 male patients, with a median age of 56 years (range 34–86 years). Tumors included 9 mixed tumors, 8 myoepitheliomas, and 1 myoepithelial carcinoma. Tumor size ranged from 0.3 to 1.7 cm (mean 1.0 cm). Mixed tumors were mostly located on the head (n=8), while myoepitheliomas arose mainly in the extremities (n=6). One myoepithelial carcinoma occurred on the cheek. Histologically, mixed tumors displayed ductal structures with epithelioid, spindle, and plasmacytoid myoepithelial cells, whereas the myoepithelial carcinoma exhibited infiltrative atypical spindle cells with pleomorphic nuclei and 5 mitoses per 10 HPF. Immunohistochemistry showed universal positivity for EMA and calponin, with variable expression of S100 (90%), cytokeratin (80%), ASMA (78%), and GFAP (50%). By FISH analysis, 7 of 16 cases (44%) exhibited EWSR1 rearrangement: 4 mixed tumors, 2 myoepitheliomas, and 1 myoepithelial carcinoma. The identification of EWSR1 rearrangements across different histologic subtypes further supports a shared molecular pathogenesis. No FUS rearrangements were detected. Follow-up data, available for 5 patients including the carcinoma case, showed no evidence of disease over 6–72 months. Overall, the authors concluded that cutaneous myoepithelial tumors form a spectrum from benign mixed tumor to myoepithelioma and myoepithelial carcinoma and that a subset harbors EWSR1 rearrangements, linking them genetically to their soft tissue, bone, and visceral counterparts.
name: EID12929

source.title: EWSR1 gene rearrangement occurs in a subset of cutaneous myoepithelial tumors: a study of 18 cases.

description: In this case report the authors described a myoepithelial carcinoma of soft tissue in a 7-week-old female infant. The tumor was located ventral to the right shoulder and measured 25 mm in diameter. Histologically, the tumor exhibited heterogeneous cytology including epithelioid, spindle, and small round cell components, embedded in a fibromyxoid stroma, with necrosis and high mitotic activity. Immunohistochemistry showed co-expression of cytokeratin (AE1/AE3), S100, and calponin, with retained INI1. Genetic analysis using FISH with EWSR1 break-apart probe and NGS panel (Archer FusionPlex Sarcoma Panel) showed the presence of the EWSR1::KLF15 fusion. Pre- and postoperative chemotherapy was administered, followed by surgical resection and proton therapy after local relapse. The patient remained disease-free two years after initial diagnosis. Overall, the authors noted that EWSR1::KLF15 is a rare fusion associated with myoepithelial tumors. It has been previously reported in only six pediatric and adolescent cases, and is associated with heterogeneous morphology and sometimes aggressive clinical behavior.
name: EID12930

source.title: Myoepithelial Carcinoma of Soft Tissue With an EWSR1-KLF15 Gene Fusion in an Infant.

description: In this report the authors described a 9-year-old boy with a myoepithelioma arising in the right posterior mediastinum. The tumor’s deep location is exceptionally rare, with only four well-documented cases reported in the literature. Histologically, the tumor exhibited features consistent with myoepithelioma, and molecular testing using next-generation sequencing revealed an EWSR1::ZNF444 fusion involving exon 7 of EWSR1 and exon 5 of ZNF444. EWSR1 fusions are a common molecular feature in soft tissue myoepitheliomas and have been reported with diverse fusion partners including PBX1, ZNF444, POU5F1, ATF1, and PBX3. Other rare alterations such as PLAG1, FUS, SRF, OGT fusions, and SMARCB1/INI1 deficiency are more frequently observed in malignant cases. This case underscores the importance of integrating histopathology with molecular genetics, particularly EWSR1 fusion status, to ensure accurate diagnosis and inform prognostic assessment.
name: EID12931

source.title: Soft Tissue Myoepithelioma in Children: A Rare Case Report of the Mediastinum and a Review of the Literature.

description: A 53-year-old Chinese man, a lifelong non-smoker, presented with chest tightness and pain. CT imaging revealed multiple small nodules in the right lower lobe of the lung. A biopsy confirmed stage IV lung adenocarcinoma with an EGFR exon 19 deletion. First-line treatment with Erlotinib (150 mg daily) resulted in a partial response, with regression of the tumors. After 28 months, disease progression was observed, characterized by enlargement of the primary tumor and the development of new bone metastases. Repeat biopsy confirmed the persistence of the EGFR exon 19 deletion along with the acquisition of a T790M mutation. The patient was subsequently treated with second-line Osimertinib (80 mg daily), achieving another partial response that lasted 15.4 months.

source.title: Presence of MET exon 14 skipping and fusion as mechanism of osimertinb resistance in a lung adenocarcinoma with an EGFR exon 19 deletion that responds to combination of capmatinib and osimertinb: A case report.

description:
This study provides robust preclinical evidence, supported by genomic data from human tumors, demonstrating that exon 4 mutations in KRAS (particularly at codon 146) represent functionally oncogenic variants.
Specifically, experimental assays show that these variants increase the active, GTP-bound fraction of KRAS, promote activation of proliferative signaling pathways, and are capable of inducing cellular transformation. In parallel, tumor-derived data indicate that these mutations recur in specific cancer types and display patterns consistent with driver events.
However, compared to classical KRAS mutations (codons 12 and 13), these variants exhibit lower levels of activation and reduced transforming capacity, suggesting a distinct mechanism of activation and a more moderate oncogenic potential.
name: EID12947

source.title: Genomic and biological characterization of exon 4 KRAS mutations in human cancer.

Cell proliferation experiments were performed in triplicate. Predictive algorithms (SIFT and PMut) predicted M737I to be tolerated.

These findings do not support FGFR3 p.S187Y as an activating oncogenic variant.

description: A 68-year-old woman presented with a painful left facial mass that was excised and pathologically diagnosed as malignant melanoma. Following surgery, she received adjuvant radiotherapy combined with temozolomide and initially experienced a favorable clinical course; however, she developed recurrent disease approximately four years later with a left parotid gland mass and regional lymph node involvement. DNA-based hybrid-capture next-generation sequencing of formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded recurrent tumor tissue identified a novel DPP10 (intergenic)::NTRK3 fusion. The report describes the breakpoint as occurring downstream of DPP10 and involving NTRK3 exon 14, although the exact fusion breakpoint is not clearly defined because the figure and text are not fully consistent. The fusion retained the NTRK3 kinase domain. Rearrangement of the NTRK3 locus was confirmed by break-apart fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH). RNA-based validation was not performed because of insufficient specimen, TRK protein expression was not evaluated by immunohistochemistry, and the patient was not treated with a TRK inhibitor.
name: EID13047

source.title: A novel DPP10 (intergenic)-NTRK3 fusion in a patient with facial malignant melanoma and potentially benefit from NTRK inhibitors.

description: Whole-exome sequencing-derived tumor mutational burden (TMB) was obtained from 75 patients recruited as part of the the CheckMate-012 trial (phase 1, open label, multicenter clincal trial of nivolumab + ipilimumab) with advanced (stage IIIB/IV) non-small cell lung carcinoma (79% non-squamous, 21% squamous) TMB was defined as the total number of nonsynonymous SNVs and indels, with high TMB classified as >158 nonsynonymous mutations (median). The primary clinical outcomes evaluated were objective response rate (ORR), durable clinical benefit (DCB), and progression-free survival (PFS). Patients with high TMB had significantly higher ORR (51% vs. 13%, p=0.0005), higher DCB (65% vs 34%, p-0.0011) and longer PFS (hazard ratio 0.41, log rank p=0.0024) compared with patients with low TMB. The authors concluded that high TMB was associated with improved clinical benefit from combined nivolumab and ipilimumab therapy in advanced NSCLC and may serve as a predictive biomarker independent of PD-L1 expression.
name: EID13103

source.title: Genomic Features of Response to Combination Immunotherapy in Patients with Advanced Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer.

description: Tumor mutational burden (TMB) derived from MSK-IMPACT targeted next-generation sequencing was evaluated in 7,894 breast cancers, from which 527 TMB-high tumors from 462 patients were identified. Tumor samples were predominantly metastatic (77%), with both primary and metastatic breast cancers included. MSK-IMPACT, a hybrid-capture sequencing assay targeting 505 cancer-associated genes (~1.2 Mb), was performed on paired tumor-normal samples with at least 10% tumor content. TMB-high was defined as ≥10 mutations/Mb. Compared with non-TMB-high breast cancers, TMB-high tumors were significantly enriched for somatic alterations in PIK3CA (60% vs. 33%; p=1.61 × 10⁻³⁷), TP53 (57% vs. 41%; p=2.36 × 10⁻¹¹), and CDH1 (34% vs. 13%; p=6.48 × 10⁻⁴³). Among 515 TMB-high tumors with available mutational-signature results, APOBEC was the predominant signature (64.7%), followed by homologous recombination deficiency (23.1%). TMB-high breast cancers were also enriched for alterations involving KMT2C, ARID1A, PTEN, NF1, and RB1 and showed a higher frequency of somatic alterations in DNA damage response and repair genes than non-TMB-high breast cancers. These findings support the classification of TMB-high breast cancer as a genomic distinct subset characterized by enrichment of specific somatic alterations and predominantly APOBEC-associated mutagenesis.
name: EID13105

source.title: Genomic characterization of tumor mutational burden-high breast carcinomas.

description: In a retrospective cohort of gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma (n = 3116; ERBB2 R678Q n = 40), ERBB2 R678Q was associated with reduced response to oxaliplatin-based regimens compared with ERBB2 WT tumors (ORR 19.0%, 95% CI 7.2 - 30.9 vs 38.0%, 95% CI 36.0 - 40.3; p = 0.03), supporting resistance to oxaliplatin-based therapy. Other ERBB2 mutations did not show reduced response (ORR 40.6%, 95% CI 29.4 - 52.9; p = 0.71 vs WT), supporting specificity of the association for R678Q.
name: EID13138

source.title: Potential Resistance to Oxaliplatin-Based Regimens in Gastric Cancer Patients with ERBB2 R678Q Mutation: Evidence from a National Genomic Database.

description: In a retrospective cohort of gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma (n = 3116; ERBB2 R678Q n = 40), ERBB2 R678Q did not show a significant association with resistance to ramucirumab-containing regimens, with ORR 9.1% (95% CI 2.5 - 26.4) compared with 13.7% (95% CI 6.8 - 25.8) for other ERBB2 mutations and 22.8% (95% CI 21.0 - 24.7) for ERBB2 WT tumors.
name: EID13139

source.title: Potential Resistance to Oxaliplatin-Based Regimens in Gastric Cancer Patients with ERBB2 R678Q Mutation: Evidence from a National Genomic Database.

description: In ex vivo human tumor slice models of mucinous cancers, GNAS-mutant tumors showed greater sensitivity to palbociclib than GNAS wild-type (WT) tumors, with significantly reduced proliferation following treatment (p = 0.028). In appendiceal peritoneal mucinous carcinomatosis (PMC) slices from three independent donors, palbociclib produced dose-dependent reductions in 5-ethynyl-2′-deoxyuridine (EdU) incorporation (200 nM, p = 0.006; 2 μM, p = 0.0002), including a 37.3-fold reduction in PanCK-positive epithelial-cell EdU incorporation in donor 229 at 2 μM (p < 0.001), supporting sensitivity to CDK4/6 inhibition.
name: EID13145

source.title: Cyclin-Dependent Kinase 4/6 Inhibition as a Novel Therapy for Peritoneal Mucinous Carcinomatosis With GNAS Mutations.

description: This paper details a prospective single-arm personalized cancer therapy study with n = 16 patients. The disease type was peritoneal mucinous carcinomatosis, predominantly of appendiceal origin. Palbociclib showed clinical activity in GNAS mutated tumors, with stable disease in 12/16 patients at 6 months and 8/10 evaluable patients at 12 months, 1-year PFS 56.2% (95% CI 36.5 - 86.7), and 1-year OS 81.2% (95% CI 64.2 - 100); median OS was NR. CEA decreased >10% in 13/16 (81%) and >50% in 6/16 (38%), while 6/11 (55%) previously treated evaluable patients had a PFS2/PFS1 ratio ≥1.3, supporting sensitivity to palbociclib.
name: EID13146

source.title: Cyclin-Dependent Kinase 4/6 Inhibition as a Novel Therapy for Peritoneal Mucinous Carcinomatosis With GNAS Mutations.

description: A patient with metastatic melanoma of unknown primary harboring an AGK-BRAF fusion with an intact BRAF kinase domain received belvarafenib 450 mg twice daily after progression on pembrolizumab, dacarbazine, and paclitaxel/carboplatin. Belvarafenib produced a confirmed partial response with a 54.5% reduction in tumor size, and the patient remained progression-free for 16.5 months before progression in pelvic soft-tissue lesions. The fusion preserved BRAF exons 8–18, including the kinase domain.
name: EID13151

source.title: Exploring Molecular Genetic Alterations and RAF Fusions in Melanoma: A Belvarafenib Expanded Access Program in Patients with RAS/RAF-Mutant Melanoma.

description: A patient with recurrent melanoma harboring a MIPOL1-RAF1 fusion with an intact RAF1 kinase domain received belvarafenib after progression following pembrolizumab with radiotherapy. Belvarafenib produced a partial response with a 32.1% reduction in abdominal wall lesions, and treatment remained ongoing at the October 2023 data cutoff. The fusion preserved RAF1 exons 8–17, including the kinase domain.
name: EID13152

source.title: Exploring Molecular Genetic Alterations and RAF Fusions in Melanoma: A Belvarafenib Expanded Access Program in Patients with RAS/RAF-Mutant Melanoma.

description: The recurrent HIST1H3B (now known as H3C2, encoding H3.1) p.K27M mutation was identified in human diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma (DIPG) samples and was associated with a significant global reduction in H3  K27 trimethylation (H3 K27me3). Using a mutation-specific antibody, Lewis et al. confirmed expression of H3.1 K27M protein in DIPG tumors and demonstrated that tumors harboring HIST1H3B K27M exhibited markedly decreased H3K27me3 compared with non-K27M tumors.
name: EID13177

source.title: Inhibition of PRC2 activity by a gain-of-function H3 mutation found in pediatric glioblastoma.

description: In a moderate-throughput functional genomic screen, FGFR3 p.H274Y demonstrated cell proliferation and viability comparable to wild-type FGFR3 in growth factor-dependent Ba/F3 and/or MCF10A cellular assays and was therefore classified as having no detectable functional impact on FGFR3-mediated cellular transformation. These findings do not support FGFR3 p.H274Y as an activating oncogenic variant.
name: EID13186

source.title: Systematic Functional Annotation of Somatic Mutations in Cancer.
